questions.questionText: A company determines that its production environment and disaster recovery (DR) environment are deployed in the same AWS Region. All production applications run on Amazon EC2 instances and are deployed through AWS CloudFormation. The applications use an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP volume for application storage. No application data is stored on the EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer copies the required AMIs to a new DR Region. The DevOps engineer also modifies the CloudFormation code to accept a Region as a parameter. Storage in the DR Region requires an RPO of 10 minutes. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 bucket in both Regions. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) for the S3 buckets. Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function to copy any new content from the FSx for ONTAP volume to the S3 bucket in the production Region.

B. Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault and a custom backup plan that has a 10-minute frequency. Specify the DR Region as the target Region. Assign the EC2 instances in the production Region to the backup plan.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function to create snapshots of the instance store volumes that are attached to the EC2 instances. Configure the Lambda function to copy the snapshots to the DR Region and to remove the previous copies. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule that invokes the Lambda function every 10 minutes.
D. Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the DR Region. Configure a 5-minute schedule for a volume-level NetApp SnapMirror to replicate the volume from the production Region to the DR Region.
questions.explanation: NetApp SnapMirror provides scheduled volume-level replication between Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file systems, including cross-Region replication. It can run as often as every 5 minutes, so replicating the application-storage volume every 5 minutes keeps the recovery point within a 10-minute RPO.
learnMore: Replicating your data using NetApp SnapMirror - FSx for ONTAP

questions.questionText: A cloud team uses AWS Organizations and AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to administer a company’s AWS accounts. The company recently formed a research team. The research team needs the ability to fully manage resources in its account, but it must not be able to create IAM users. The cloud team creates a Research Administrator permission set in IAM Identity Center for the research team. The permission set has the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy attached. The cloud team must ensure that nobody on the research team can create IAM users. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM policy that denies the iam:CreateUser action. Attach the IAM policy to the Research Administrator permission set.
B. Create an IAM policy that allows all actions except the iam:CreateUser action. Use the IAM policy to set the permissions boundary for the Research Administrator permission set.
C. Create an SCP that denies the iam:CreateUser action. Attach the SCP to the research team's AWS account.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes IAM users. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that detects the IAM CreateUser event. Configure the rule to invoke the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: An SCP with an explicit Deny for iam:CreateUser restricts every principal in the affected member account and overrides permissions granted by AdministratorAccess. It cannot be bypassed by creating and assuming another IAM role, unlike a deny policy or permissions boundary applied only to the IAM Identity Center permission-set role.
learnMore: Service control policies (SCPs)
Permissions boundaries for IAM entities

questions.questionText: A company operates several applications in the same AWS account. The applications send logs to Amazon CloudWatch. A data analytics team must collect performance metrics and custom metrics from the applications. The team must transform the metrics data before storing it in an Amazon S3 bucket. The team must automatically collect any new metrics that are added to the CloudWatch namespace. Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Configure a CloudWatch metric stream to include metrics from the application and the CloudWatch namespace. Configure the metric stream to deliver the metrics to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the Firehose delivery stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform the data. Configure the delivery stream to send the transformed data to the S3 bucket.

B. Configure a CloudWatch metrics stream to include all the metrics and to deliver the metrics to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the Firehose delivery stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform the data. Configure the delivery stream to send the transformed data to the S3 bucket.
C. Configure metric filters for the CloudWatch logs to create custom metrics. Configure a CloudWatch metric stream to deliver the application metrics to the S3 bucket.

D. Configure subscription filters on the application log groups to target an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the Firehose delivery stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform the data. Configure the delivery stream to send the transformed data to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: A CloudWatch metric stream configured for all metrics automatically includes newly created metrics. It can send metrics to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream, where an AWS Lambda transformation is applied before Firehose delivers the transformed records to Amazon S3. This avoids maintaining filters or subscriptions as metrics are added.
learnMore: Use metric streams - Amazon CloudWatch
Custom setup with Firehose - Amazon CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A company deploys an application across two AWS Regions. The application creates and stores objects in an Amazon S3 bucket in the same Region as the application. Both application deployments must access every object and its metadata from both Regions. The company has configured two-way replication between the S3 buckets and enabled S3 Replication metrics on each bucket. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that retries replication when an object fails to replicate. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that listens to S3 event notifications for failed replication events. Create an AWS Lambda function that downloads the failed replication object and then runs a PutObject command for the object to the destination bucket. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function to handle the object that failed to replicate.

B. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure S3 event notifications to send failed replication notifications to the SQS queue. Create an AWS Lambda function that downloads the failed replication object and then runs a PutObject command for the object to the destination bucket. Configure the Lambda function to poll the queue for notifications to process.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that listens to S3 event notifications for failed replications. Create an AWS Lambda function that downloads the failed replication object and then runs a PutObject command for the object to the destination bucket.

D. Create an AWS Lambda function that will use S3 batch operations to retry the replication on the existing object for a failed replication. Configure S3 event notifications to send failed replication notifications to the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 sends s3:Replication:OperationFailedReplication notifications for failed replication when replication metrics are enabled. Objects whose live replication has failed must be replicated again with S3 Batch Replication; a Batch Replication job can target objects with the FAILED replication status. A Lambda function invoked by the failure notification can initiate the required S3 Batch Operations retry.
learnMore: Getting replication status information - Amazon S3
Replicating existing objects with Batch Replication - Amazon S3

questions.questionText: A company mandates that its internal business teams launch resources only by using pre-approved AWS CloudFormation templates. The security team requires automated monitoring when resources deviate from their expected state. Which strategy should be used to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Allow users to deploy CloudFormation stacks using a CloudFormation service role only. Use CloudFormation drift detection to detect when resources have drifted from their expected state.
B. Allow users to deploy CloudFormation stacks using a CloudFormation service role only. Use AWS Config rules to detect when resources have drifted from their expected state.

C. Allow users to deploy CloudFormation stacks using AWS Service Catalog only. Enforce the use of a launch constraint. Use AWS Config rules to detect when resources have drifted from their expected state.

D. Allow users to deploy CloudFormation stacks using AWS Service Catalog only. Enforce the use of a template constraint. Use Amazon EventBridge notifications to detect when resources have drifted from their expected state.
questions.explanation: AWS Service Catalog presents administrator-approved AWS CloudFormation templates as products, ensuring teams provision only approved offerings. A launch constraint specifies the IAM role that Service Catalog assumes to provision a product, while AWS Config rules continuously evaluate resource configurations and flag resources as noncompliant when configuration changes violate the defined requirements.
learnMore: Components of an AWS Config Rule

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must design a cloud-based solution to standardize deployment artifacts for AWS Cloud deployments and on-premises deployments. Currently, no traffic routing exists between the on-premises data center and the AWS environment. The solution must be able to consume downstream packages from public repositories and be highly available. Data must be encrypted both in transit and at rest. The solution must store deployment artifacts in object storage and deploy the artifacts to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Deployment artifacts must be encrypted in transit when they travel over the public internet. The DevOps engineer must deploy this solution in less than two weeks. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: B. Use an AWS Direct Connect connection and a VPN connection to connect the on-premises data center to AWS. Deploy third-party artifact management software on Amazon EC2 instances.
C. Use two AWS VPN connections to connect the on-premises data center to AWS. Use AWS CodeArtifact to store the deployment artifacts.
D. Use parallel AWS Direct Connect connections to connect the on-premises data center to AWS. Deploy third-party artifact management software on Amazon EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeArtifact is a managed, highly scalable artifact repository that can obtain packages from external public repositories through external connections and upstream repositories. Its package assets are encrypted at rest with AWS KMS, and communication with CodeArtifact is protected by TLS. Two AWS VPN connections provide redundant, encrypted connectivity between the on-premises environment and AWS and can be deployed far more quickly than Direct Connect. This avoids the operational overhead and availability risk of operating third-party artifact-management software on EC2 instances.
learnMore: What is AWS CodeArtifact?
Data encryption in AWS CodeArtifact

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Question 77 / Resilient Cloud Solutions A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application handles a high volume of messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. A DevOps engineer observes that the application required several hours to process a group of messages from the SQS queue. While processing the messages, the Auto Scaling group's average CPU utilization did not exceed the threshold configured in a target tracking scaling policy. The application that processes the SQS queue sends logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The DevOps engineer must ensure the queue is processed quickly. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to publish a custom metric by using the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible SQS queue attribute and the GroupInServiceInstances Auto Scaling group attribute to publish the queue messages for each instance. Schedule an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function every hour. Create a target tracking scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group that uses the custom metric to scale in and out.

B. Create an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to publish a custom metric by using the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible SQS queue attribute and the GroupInServiceInstances Auto Scaling group attribute to publish the queue messages for each instance. Create a CloudWatch subscription filter for the application logs with the Lambda function as the target. Create a target tracking scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group that uses the custom metric to scale in and out.

C. Create a target tracking scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. In the target tracking policy, use the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible SQS queue attribute and the GroupInServiceInstances Auto Scaling group attribute to calculate how many messages are in the queue for each number of instances by using metric math. Use the calculated attribute to scale in and out.

D. Create an AWS Lambda function that logs the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible attribute of the SQS queue to a CloudWatch Logs log group. Schedule an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function every 5 minutes. Create a metric filer to count the number of log events from a CloudWatch logs group. Create a target tracking scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group that uses the custom metric to scale in and out.
questions.explanation: For SQS consumers, queue depth alone does not scale proportionally with fleet size, and CPU utilization might not reflect message backlog. A target tracking policy can use CloudWatch metric math to calculate backlog per instance by dividing ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible by GroupInServiceInstances, allowing the Auto Scaling group to scale directly with the processing workload without maintaining Lambda functions or custom metrics.
learnMore: Create a target tracking scaling policy using metric math
Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage its AWS accounts. The company’s automation account includes a CI/CD pipeline that creates and configures new AWS accounts. The company has a group of internal service teams that deliver services to accounts in the organization. The service teams work from a set of service accounts. They want to receive an AWS CloudTrail event in their service accounts when the CreateAccount API call creates a new account. How should the company share this CloudTrail event with the service accounts?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule in the automation account to send account creation events to the default event bus in the services accounts. Update the default event bus in the services accounts to allow events from the automation account.

B. Create a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus in the services accounts. Update the custom event bus to allow events from the automation account. Create an EventBridge rule in the services account that directly listens to CloudTrail events from the automation account.

C. Create a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus in the automation account and the services accounts. Create an EventBridge rule and policy that connects the custom event buses that are in the automation account and the services accounts.

D. Create a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus in the automation account. Create an EventBridge rule and policy that connects the custom event bus to the default event buses in the services accounts.
questions.explanation: CloudTrail API-call events are delivered to the default EventBridge event bus. An EventBridge rule in the automation account can match the CreateAccount event and send it to the default event bus in each service account. Each destination event bus must have a resource-based policy that permits the automation account to publish events. Custom event buses do not receive CloudTrail events directly.

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer updates an AWS CloudFormation stack to add a nested stack containing several Amazon EC2 instances. When the DevOps engineer tries to deploy the updated stack, the nested stack does not deploy successfully. What should the DevOps engineer do to identify the cause of the failure?
options: A. Use the CloudFormation detect root cause capability for the failed stack to analyze the failure and return the event that is the most likely cause for the failure.
B. Query failed stacks by specifying the root stack as the ParentId property. Examine the StackStatusReason property for all returned stacks to determine the reason the nested stack failed to deploy.

C. Activate AWS Systems Manager for the AWS account where the application runs. Use the AWS Systems Manager Automation AWS-SupportTroubleshootCFNCustomResource runbook to determine the reason the nested stack failed to deploy.

D. Configure the CloudFormation template to publish logs to Amazon CloudWatch. View the CloudFormation logs for the failed stack in the CloudWatch console to determine the reason the nested stack failed to deploy.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation does not support the Detect root cause capability for nested stacks. For a nested stack, ParentId identifies its direct parent, and StackStatusReason contains the success or failure message associated with its status. Reviewing the failed nested stacks associated with the root stack and their status reasons identifies the deployment failure.
learnMore: Determine the cause of a stack failure - AWS CloudFormation
StackSummary - AWS CloudFormation API Reference

questions.questionText: A DevOps administrator is setting up a repository to store a company’s container images. The administrator must configure a lifecycle rule that automatically deletes container images with a specific tag when they are older than 15 days. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create a repository in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Add a lifecycle policy to the repository to expire images that have the matching tag after 15 days.
B. Create a repository in AWS CodeArtifact. Add a repository policy to the CodeArtifact repository to expire old assets that have the matching tag after 15 days.
C. Create a bucket in Amazon S3. Add a bucket lifecycle policy to expire old objects that have the matching tag after 15 days
D. Create an EC2 Image Builder container recipe. Add a build component to expire the container that has the matching tag after 15 days.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR is purpose-built for storing container images and provides repository lifecycle policies. A rule can target tagged images through a tag pattern or prefix and use an age-based expiration criterion to delete images that have been pushed for more than the specified number of days, requiring no custom cleanup process.
learnMore: Lifecycle policy properties in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A DevOps engineer created an AWS CloudFormation template that deploys an application on Amazon EC2 instances. Question 81 / Configuration Management and IaC A DevOps engineer created an AWS CloudFormation template that deploys an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances run Amazon Linux. Shell scripts contained in user data deploy the application to the EC2 instances. The EC2 instances use an IAM instance profile with an IAM role that has the AmazonSSMManagedinstanceCore managed policy attached. The DevOps engineer changed the user data in the CloudFormation template to install a new version of the application and applied the stack update. However, the application did not update on the running EC2 instances. The engineer must ensure that application changes are installed on the running EC2 instances. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Configure the user data content to use the Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) multipart format. Set the scripts-user parameter to always in the text/cloud-config section.
B. Refactor the user data commands to use the cfn-init helper script. Update the user data to install and configure the cfn-hup and cfn-init helper scripts to monitor and apply the metadata changes.

C. Configure an EC2 launch template for the EC2 instances. Create a new EC2 Auto Scaling group. Associate the Auto Scaling group with the EC2 launch template. Use the AutoScalingScheduledAction update policy for the Auto Scaling group.

D. Refactor the user data commands to use an AWS Systems Manager document (SSM document). Add an AWS CLI command in the user data to use Systems Manager Run Command to apply the SSM document to the EC2 instances.
E. Refactor the user data command to use an AWS Systems Manager document (SSM document). Use Systems Manager State Manager to create an association between the SSM document and the EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: The cfn-hup daemon detects changes to CloudFormation resource metadata after a stack update and can invoke cfn-init to apply revised AWS::CloudFormation::Init configuration on running EC2 instances. Systems Manager State Manager associations apply an SSM document to targeted managed nodes and can enforce the updated application configuration without replacing the instances.
learnMore: cfn-hup - AWS CloudFormation
Association - AWS Systems Manager API Reference

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company operates an application on Amazon EC2 instances. Question 82 / SDLC Automation A company operates an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company uses a series of AWS CloudFormation stacks to define the application resources. A developer makes updates by building and testing the application on a laptop, then uploading the build output and CloudFormation stack templates to Amazon S3. The developer’s peers review the changes before the developer updates the CloudFormation stacks and installs a new application version on the EC2 instances. The deployment process is error-prone and time-consuming because the developer updates every EC2 instance with the new application. The company wants to automate as much of the application deployment process as possible while retaining a final manual approval step before any application or resource modification. The company has already moved the application source code and CloudFormation templates to AWS CodeCommit. The company has also created an AWS CodeBuild project to build and test the application. Which combination of steps will meet the company’s requirements? Choose two
options: A. Create an application group and a deployment group in AWS CodeDeploy. Install the CodeDeploy agent on the EC2 instances.
B. Create an application revision and a deployment group in AWS CodeDeploy. Create an environment in CodeDeploy. Register the EC2 instances to the CodeDeploy environment.
C. Use AWS CodePipeline to invoke the CodeBuild job, run the CloudFormation update, and pause for a manual approval step. After approval, start the AWS CodeDeploy deployment.

D. Use AWS CodePipeline to invoke the CodeBuild job, create CloudFormation change sets for each of the application stacks, and pause for a manual approval step. After approval, run the CloudFormation change sets and start the AWS CodeDeploy deployment.

E. Use AWS CodePipeline to invoke the CodeBuild job, create CloudFormation change sets for each of the application stacks, and pause for a manual approval step. After approval, start the AWS CodeDeploy deployment.
questions.explanation: For Amazon EC2 deployments, AWS CodeDeploy uses an application and a deployment group to target instances, which require the CodeDeploy agent. AWS CodePipeline can build with CodeBuild, create CloudFormation change sets so proposed resource modifications can be reviewed without changing the stacks, pause at a manual approval action, and, upon approval, execute the change sets and initiate the CodeDeploy deployment.
learnMore: CloudFormation deploy action reference
Add a manual approval action to a stage

questions.questionText: A company has migrated its container-based applications to Amazon EKS and wants to set up automated email notifications. Notifications sent to each email address relate to specific activities involving EKS components. The solution will use Amazon SNS topics and an AWS Lambda function to assess incoming log events and publish messages to the appropriate SNS topic. Which logging solution supports these requirements?
options: A. Enable Amazon CloudWatch Logs to log the EKS components. Create a CloudWatch subscription filter for each component with Lambda as the subscription feed destination.
B. Enable Amazon CloudWatch Logs to log the EKS components. Create CloudWatch Logs Insights queries linked to Amazon EventBridge events that invoke Lambda.
C. Enable Amazon S3 logging for the EKS components. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch subscription filter for each component with Lambda as the subscription feed destination.
D. Enable Amazon S3 logging for the EKS components. Configure S3 PUT Object event notifications with AWS Lambda as the destination.
questions.explanation: Amazon EKS control-plane logs are delivered to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, where CloudWatch Logs subscription filters can forward matching log events to AWS Lambda in near real time. Lambda can evaluate the component-specific events and publish notification messages to the corresponding Amazon SNS topics.
learnMore: Send control plane logs to CloudWatch Logs - Amazon EKS
Log group-level subscription filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts. Question 84 / Configuration Management and IaC A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts. The company has enabled all features for the organization. The company configured the organization as a hierarchy of OUs beneath the root OU. The company recently registered all of its OUs and enrolled all of its AWS accounts in AWS Control Tower. The company must customize the AWS Control Tower-managed AWS Config configuration recorder in each company AWS account. The company must apply these customizations to both the existing AWS accounts and any new AWS accounts that it enrolls in AWS Control Tower in the future. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Create a new AWS account. Create an AWS Lambda function in the new account to apply the customizations to the AWS Config configuration recorder in each AWS account in the organization.

B. Create a new AWS account as an AWS Config delegated administrator. Create an AWS Lambda function in the delegated administrator account to apply the customizations to the AWS Config configuration recorder in the delegated administrator account.

C. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule in the AWS Control Tower management account to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the Organizations OU is registered or reregistered. Re-register the root Organizations OU.

D. Configure the AWSControlTowerExecution IAM role in each AWS account in the organization to be assumable by an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to assume the AWSControlTowerExecution IAM role.

E. Create an IAM role in the AWS Control Tower management account that an AWS Lambda function can assume. Grant the IAM role permission to assume the AWSControlTowerExecution IAM role in any account in the organization. Configure the Lambda function to use the new IAM role.
questions.explanation: An EventBridge rule in the AWS Control Tower management account can invoke automation for account enrollment, account updates, and landing-zone updates; re-registering each OU causes the existing enrolled accounts to be updated. A Lambda execution role in the management account needs permission to assume AWSControlTowerExecution in each member account, and the target roles must trust the Lambda-based cross-account access. The assumed AWSControlTowerExecution role can update each account’s AWS Config configuration recorder, while the lifecycle events apply the customization to future accounts as they are enrolled.
learnMore: Guidance for Customizing AWS Config Resources in AWS Control Tower
The AWSControlTowerExecution role, explained

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company uses AWS CodeDeploy to automate software deployments. Question 85 / SDLC Automation A company uses AWS CodeDeploy to automate software deployments. The deployment must satisfy these requirements: Several instances must remain available to serve traffic during deployment. Traffic must be balanced across those instances, and the instances must automatically recover if a failure occurs. A new fleet of instances must be automatically launched to deploy a new revision, without manual provisioning. Traffic must be rerouted to the new environment for half of the new instances at a time. The deployment must succeed if traffic is rerouted to at least half of the instances; otherwise, it must fail. Before traffic is routed to the new fleet of instances, temporary files created during the deployment process must be deleted. At the completion of a successful deployment, the original instances in the deployment group must be deleted immediately to reduce costs. How can a DevOps engineer fulfill these requirements?
options: A. Use an Application Load Balancer and an in-place deployment. Associate the Auto Scaling group with the deployment group. Use the Automatically copy Auto Scaling group option, and use CodeDeployDefault.OneAtAtime as the deployment configuration. Instruct AWS CodeDeploy to terminate the original instances in the deployment group, and use the AllowTraffic hook within appspec.yml to delete the temporary files.

B. Use an Application Load Balancer and a blue/green deployment. Associate the Auto Scaling group and Application Load Balancer target group with the deployment group. Use the Automatically copy Auto Scaling group option, create a custom deployment configuration with minimum healthy hosts defined as 50%, and assign the configuration to the deployment group. Instruct AWS CodeDeploy to terminate the original instances in the deployment group, and use the BeforeBlockTraffic hook within appspec.yml to delete the temporary files.

C. Use an Application Load Balancer and a blue/green deployment. Associate the Auto Scaling group and the Application Load Balancer target group with the deployment group. Use the Automatically copy Auto Scaling group option, and use CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtAtime as the deployment configuration. Instruct AWS CodeDeploy to terminate the original instances in the deployment group, and use the BeforeAllowTraffic hook within appspec.yml to delete the temporary files.

D. Use an Application Load Balancer and an in-place deployment. Associate the Auto Scaling group and Application Load Balancer target group with the deployment group. Use the Automatically copy Auto Scaling group option, and use CodeDeployDefault.AllatOnce as a deployment configuration. Instruct AWS CodeDeploy to terminate the original instances in the deployment group, and use the BlockTraffic hook within appspec.yml to delete the temporary files.
questions.explanation: An EC2 blue/green deployment that automatically copies the Auto Scaling group creates a replacement fleet while the original fleet continues serving load-balanced traffic. CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime routes traffic to up to half of the replacement instances at a time and succeeds if rerouting succeeds for at least half. The BeforeAllowTraffic AppSpec lifecycle hook runs on replacement instances before they are registered with the load balancer, making it the proper point to remove temporary deployment files. Configuring termination of the original instances with no wait period removes the old fleet immediately after successful traffic rerouting. Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy AppSpec 'hooks' section
learnMore: Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy
AppSpec 'hooks' section

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS CodePipeline pipeline to deploy an application. The company created an AWS Fault Injection Service (AWS FIS) experiment template to test the application's resilience. A DevOps engineer must integrate the experiment into the pipeline. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Configure a new stage in the pipeline that includes an AWS FIS action. Configure the action to reference the AWS FIS experiment template. Grant the pipeline access to start the experiment.

B. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduler. Grant the scheduler permission to start the AWS FIS experiment. Configure a new stage in the pipeline that includes an action to invoke the EventBridge scheduler.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function to start the AWS FIS experiment. Grant the Lambda function permission to start the experiment. Create a new stage in the pipeline that has a Lambda action. Set the action to invoke the Lambda function.

D. Export the AWS FIS experiment template to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS CodeBuild unit test project that has a buildspec that starts the AWS FIS experiment. Grant the CodeBuild project access to start the experiment. Configure a new stage in the pipeline that includes an action to run the CodeBuild unit test project.
questions.explanation: AWS FIS starts an experiment through the StartExperiment API using the experiment template ID. AWS CodePipeline can invoke a Lambda function as a pipeline action; therefore, a Lambda function granted fis:StartExperiment permission can start the AWS FIS experiment during a new pipeline stage.
learnMore: StartExperiment - AWS Fault Injection Service

questions.questionText: A company has recently migrated its legacy application from on premises to AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer, which is behind Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to ensure that users have minimal disruption during deployments of a new application version. The company also wants to be able to roll back updates quickly if an issue occurs. Which solution meets these requirements with MINIMAL application changes?
options: A. Introduce changes as a separate environment parallel to the existing one. Configure API Gateway to use a canary release deployment to send a small subset of user traffic to the new environment.
B. Introduce changes as a separate environment parallel to the existing one. Update the application’s DNS alias records to point to the new environment.
C. Introduce changes as a separate target group behind the existing Application Load Balancer. Configure API Gateway to route user traffic to the new target group in steps.

D. Introduce changes as a separate target group behind the existing Application Load Balancer. Configure API Gateway to route all traffic to the Application Load Balancer, which then sends the traffic to the new target group.
questions.explanation: Amazon API Gateway canary releases route a configurable small percentage of requests to a new deployment while the existing production deployment continues to receive the remaining traffic. A parallel environment can be selected for the canary through stage-variable overrides, enabling a gradual rollout and fast rollback by setting canary traffic to zero. API Gateway does not route requests directly to individual Application Load Balancer target groups.
learnMore: Set up an API Gateway canary release deployment
Create a canary release deployment

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company uses a CI/CD pipeline to deploy its workload in the ap-southeast-2 Region. Question 88 / Resilient Cloud Solutions A company uses a CI/CD pipeline to deploy its workload in the ap-southeast-2 Region. The company receives images by way of a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and processes those images in AWS Fargate tasks on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. An Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository stores the images as Docker images. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to configure DNS. The company stores the images in an Amazon S3 bucket and stores image metadata in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to extend the workload into a second Region. A DevOps engineer must create a highly available and resilient design that expands the workload to the eu-west-2 Region. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the fewest configuration changes? Choose three
options: A. Configure ECR replication to eu-west-2 on the repository. Configure an NLB in eu-west-2 that resolves to Fargate tasks in an ECS cluster in eu-west-2. Configure a latency routing policy in Route 53 for the two workloads.
B. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table with a replica in eu-west-2. Configure the Fargate tasks to interact with the DynamoDB table in ap-southeast-2.
C. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table with a replica in eu-west-2. Configure the Fargate tasks to interact with the DynamoDB table in the same Region that the tasks run in.

D. Configure a new S3 bucket in eu-west-2. Configure data replication between the S3 bucket in ap-southeast-2 and the S3 bucket in eu-west-2. Configure the Fargate tasks to use the S3 bucket in the same Region that the tasks run in to perform S3 PUT operations and GET operations.

E. Configure an S3 Multi-Region Access Point for the S3 bucket in ap-southeast-2 and a new S3 bucket in eu-west-2. Configure two-way replication on the S3 buckets. Configure the workloads to use the Multi-Region Access Point for S3 PUT operations and GET operations.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR supports cross-Region replication, allowing the existing image repository to supply the second Region without changing the CI/CD pipeline. Route 53 latency-based routing can route requests to Regional load balancers based on the lowest-latency Region. DynamoDB global tables replicate data across Regions, and AWS recommends that an application access the local Regional DynamoDB endpoint. An S3 Multi-Region Access Point provides a single global endpoint that routes requests to the closest active Region; two-way replication keeps objects written in either Regional bucket synchronized.
learnMore: Private image replication in Amazon ECR
Using DynamoDB global tables

questions.questionText: A company operates a multi-tenant environment in its VPC and has configured Amazon GuardDuty for the related AWS account. The company forwards all GuardDuty findings to AWS Security Hub. Traffic from suspicious sources is producing a high volume of findings. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that automatically denies traffic throughout the VPC when GuardDuty identifies a new suspicious source. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a GuardDuty threat list. Configure GuardDuty to reference the list. Create an AWS Lambda function that will update the threat list. Configure the Lambda function to run in response to new Security Hub findings that come from GuardDuty.

B. Configure an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a custom rule group. Create an AWS Lambda function that will create a block rule in the custom rule group. Configure the Lambda function to run in response to new Security Hub findings that come from GuardDuty.

C. Configure a firewall in AWS Network Firewall. Create an AWS Lambda function that will create a Drop action rule in the firewall policy. Configure the Lambda function to run in response to new Security Hub findings that come from GuardDuty.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that will create a GuardDuty suppression rule. Configure the Lambda function to run in response to new Security Hub findings that come from GuardDuty.
questions.explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall for VPC traffic. Its firewall policy can contain rules that match a source and use the DROP action to block matching packets from reaching their destinations. A Lambda function invoked for new GuardDuty-originated Security Hub findings can add the identified suspicious source to such a rule, providing VPC-wide enforcement when the VPC routes traffic through the firewall. GuardDuty threat lists only influence detection, AWS WAF applies to web resources, and suppression rules only reduce finding visibility.
learnMore: What is AWS Network Firewall?
Defining rule actions in AWS Network Firewall

questions.questionText: A company has an AWS CloudFormation stack deployed in one AWS account. The company configured the stack to send event notifications to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. A DevOps engineer must implement an automated solution that applies a tag to the particular CloudFormation stack instance only after a successful stack update. The DevOps engineer has created an AWS Lambda function that applies and updates this tag for that specific stack instance. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Run the AWS-UpdateCloudFormationStack AWS Systems ManagerAutomation runbook when Systems Manager detects an UPDATE_COMPLETE event for the instance status of the CloudFormation stack. Configure the runbook to invoke the Lambda function.

B. Create a custom AWS Config rule that produces a compliance change event if the CloudFormation stack has an UPDATE_COMPLETE instance status. Configure AWS Config to directly invoke the Lambda function to automatically remediate the change event.
C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches the UPDATE_COMPLETE event pattern for the instance status of the CloudFormation stack. Configure the rule to invoke the Lambda function.
D. Adjust the configuration of the CloudFormation stack to send notifications for only an UPDATE_COMPLETE instance status event to the SNS topic. Subscribe the Lambda function to the SNS topic.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation publishes CloudFormation Stack Status Change events to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can match the UPDATE_COMPLETE status and invoke the Lambda function; the event includes the stack ID, allowing the function to tag only the stack whose update completed successfully. CloudFormation SNS notification ARNs publish stack-related events rather than supporting a configuration limited to only UPDATE_COMPLETE.
learnMore: Stack Status Change event detail - AWS CloudFormation

questions.questionText: A security assessment found that an AWS CodeBuild project downloads a database population script from an Amazon S3 bucket through an unauthenticated request. The security team prohibits unauthenticated requests to S3 buckets for this project. How can this issue be remediated in the MOST secure way?
options: A. Add the bucket name to the AllowedBuckets section of the CodeBuild project settings. Update the build spec to use the AWS CLI to download the database population script.
B. Modify the S3 bucket settings to enable HTTPS basic authentication and specify a token. Update the build spec to use cURL to pass the token and download the database population script.

C. Remove unauthenticated access from the S3 bucket with a bucket policy. Modify the service role for the CodeBuild project to include Amazon S3 access. Use the AWS CLI to download the database population script.
D. Remove unauthenticated access from the S3 bucket with a bucket policy. Use the AWS CLI to download the database population script using an IAM access key and a secret access key.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild performs actions on behalf of a build by using its service role. Removing anonymous bucket access and granting that role only the necessary S3 read permission allows the AWS CLI to use temporary role credentials, avoiding publicly accessible objects and embedded long-lived access keys. AWS recommends that CodeBuild service roles follow least privilege and can be scoped to specific resources.
learnMore: Allow CodeBuild to interact with other AWS services
Identity and access management in AWS CodeBuild

questions.questionText: A video-sharing company keeps its videos in Amazon S3. It has noticed a sudden rise in video access requests, but does not know which videos are most popular. The company needs to determine the overall access pattern for the video files. This pattern includes the number of users who access a particular file on a given day, along with the number of pull requests for particular files. How can the company satisfy these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?
options: A. Activate S3 server access logging. Import the access logs into an Amazon Aurora database. Use an Aurora SQL query to analyze the access patterns.
B. Activate S3 server access logging. Use Amazon Athena to create an external table with the log files. Use Athena to create a SQL query to analyze the access patterns.

C. Invoke an AWS Lambda function for every S3 object access event. Configure the Lambda function to write the file access information, such as user. S3 bucket, and file key, to an Amazon Aurora database. Use an Aurora SQL query to analyze the access patterns.

D. Record an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log message for every S3 object access event. Configure a CloudWatch Logs log stream to write the file access information, such as user, S3 bucket, and file key, to an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL application. Perform a sliding window analysis.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 server access logging provides records of requests made to a bucket, including request time, requester, object key, and operation. Amazon Athena can query those log objects directly in Amazon S3 through an external table, so SQL aggregations can determine unique users and request counts per file and day without loading the logs into or maintaining a separate database. AWS: Using Amazon S3 server access logs to identify requests
learnMore: Using Amazon S3 server access logs to identify requests
Logging requests with server access logging

questions.questionText: A company follows a trunk-based development branching strategy. It has two AWS CodePipeline pipelines that integrate with a Git provider. The pull_request pipeline has a branch filter matching the feature branches. The main_branch pipeline has a branch filter matching the main branch. When pull requests merge into the main branch, they are deployed through the main_branch pipeline. The company’s developers need test results for every submitted pull request as quickly as possible from the pull_request pipeline. The company must ensure that the main_branch pipeline’s test results complete and that each deployment finishes before the next pipeline execution. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure the pull_request pipeline to use PARALLEL mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use QUEUED mode.
B. Configure the pull_request pipeline to use SUPERSEDED mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use QUEUED mode.
C. Configure the pull_request pipeline to use PARALLEL mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use SUPERSEDED mode
D. Configure the pull_request pipeline to use QUEUED mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use SUPERSEDED mode.
questions.explanation: AWS CodePipeline PARALLEL mode runs executions simultaneously and independently, allowing all pull-request test runs to proceed without waiting for one another. QUEUED mode processes executions one at a time in the order queued, so a main-branch execution’s tests and deployment complete before the next execution starts.
learnMore: How pipeline executions work - AWS CodePipeline
Set or change the pipeline execution mode - AWS CodePipeline

questions.questionText: A company wants to reduce the time required to develop new features. It uses AWS CodeBuild and AWS CodeDeploy to build and deploy applications, and uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy each microservice through its own CI/CD pipeline. The company needs greater visibility into the average time between new-feature releases and the average time to recover after a failed deployment. Which solution provides this visibility with the LEAST configuration effort?
options: A. Program an AWS Lambda function that creates Amazon CloudWatch custom metrics with information about successful runs and failed runs for each pipeline. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes. Use the metrics to build a CloudWatch dashboard.

B. Program an AWS Lambda function that creates Amazon CloudWatch custom metrics with information about successful runs and failed runs for each pipeline. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function after every successful run and after every failed run. Use the metrics to build a CloudWatch dashboard.

C. Program an AWS Lambda function that writes information about successful runs and failed runs to Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function after every successful run and after every failed run. Build an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to show the information from DynamoDB.

D. Program an AWS Lambda function that writes information about successful runs and failed runs to Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes. Build an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to show the information from DynamoDB.
questions.explanation: AWS CodePipeline sends pipeline execution state-change events, including SUCCEEDED and FAILED, directly to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can invoke AWS Lambda as each state change occurs, allowing the function to publish time-based success and failure/recovery data as Amazon CloudWatch custom metrics. A CloudWatch dashboard can visualize those metrics without adding a separate data store and BI service. Event-driven collection also avoids the polling and execution-discovery logic required by a five-minute schedule.
learnMore: Monitoring CodePipeline events
CodePipeline CloudWatch metrics

questions.questionText: A company is developing code and plans to use semantic versioning. The company's DevOps team must create a pipeline to compile the code. The team must also manage versions of the compiled code. If the code uses open-source libraries, those libraries must also be cached during the build process. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS CodeArtifact repository and associate the upstream repositories. Create an AWS CodeBuild project that builds the semantic version of the code artifacts. Configure the project to authenticate and connect to the CodeArtifact repository and publish the artifact to the repository.
B. Use AWS CodeDeploy to upload the generated semantic version of the artifact to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
C. Use an AWS CodeBuild project to build the code and to publish the generated semantic version of the artifact to AWS Artifact. Configure build caching in the CodeBuild project.

D. Create a new AWS CodeArtifact repository. Create an AWS Lambda function that pulls open source packages from the internet and publishes the packages to the repository. Configure AWS CodeDeploy to build semantic versions of the code and publish the versions to the repository.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild compiles source code and executes the build commands needed to create semantic package versions. AWS CodeArtifact stores and publishes versioned software packages, and its upstream/external repository support lets builds retrieve open-source dependencies through a repository endpoint while retaining fetched packages for reuse. A CodeBuild project can authenticate to CodeArtifact and publish the generated artifact there.
learnMore: What is AWS CodeBuild?
What is AWS CodeArtifact?

questions.questionText: A company needs to make sure that its EC2 instances are secure. It wants notification whenever new vulnerabilities are discovered on the instances, and it also needs an audit trail for all instance login activity. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager to detect vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances. Install the Amazon Kinesis Agent to capture system logs and deliver them to Amazon S3.
B. Use AWS Systems Manager to detect vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances. Install the Systems Manager Agent to capture system logs and view login activity in the CloudTrail console.
C. Configure Amazon CloudWatch to detect vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances. Install the AWS Config daemon to capture system logs and view them in the AWS Config console.
D. Configure Amazon Inspector to detect vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances. Install the Amazon CloudWatch Agent to capture system logs and record them via Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector continuously assesses Amazon EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and creates findings when a relevant vulnerability is detected, including when a new applicable CVE is added. The Amazon CloudWatch agent can collect log files from EC2 instances and send them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs; configuring it to collect operating-system authentication logs provides a retained audit trail of login activity.
learnMore: Scanning Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Inspector
Understanding Amazon Inspector findings

questions.questionText: A security team must capture AWS resource configurations, identify issues, and send notifications about findings. The primary workload in the AWS account is an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group that scales out and in several times each day. The team requires notification within 2 days whenever an Amazon EC2 security group permits traffic on port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0. The team also requires routine snapshots of AWS resource configurations. The security team has already created an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic and subscribed to it. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Config to use periodic recording for the AWS account. Deploy the vpc-sg-port-restriction-check AWS Config managed rule. Configure AWS Config to use the SNS topic as the target for notifications.

B. Configure AWS Config to use configuration change recording for the AWS account. Deploy the vpc-sg-open-only-to-authorized-ports AWS Config managed rule. Configure AWS Config to use the SNS topic as the target for notifications.

C. Configure AWS Config to use configuration change recording for the AWS account. Deploy the ssh-restricted AWS Config managed rule. Configure AWS Config to use the SNS topic as the target for notifications.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function to evaluate security groups and publish a message to the SNS topic. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule the Lambda function to run once a day.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule vpc-sg-port-restriction-check marks a security group noncompliant when it allows unrestricted traffic on TCP/UDP port 22 by default. It runs periodically, so it can detect and notify on the exposure within the required 2 days through the SNS topic. AWS Config daily recording produces a configuration item representing the latest resource state over a 24-hour period when it has changed, providing routine configuration snapshots while avoiding a record for every Auto Scaling event.
learnMore: Recording AWS resources with AWS Config

questions.questionText: A company operates an event-driven JavaScript application. The application uses decoupled AWS managed services that publish, consume, and route events. During application testing, events are not being delivered to the target specified by an Amazon EventBridge rule. A DevOps team must give application testers additional functionality to view and troubleshoot events, and to prevent event loss, without redeploying the application. Which combination of steps should the DevOps team take to meet these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Launch AWS Device Farm with a standard test environment and project to run a specific build of the application.
B. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable AWS CloudTrail. Create a CloudTrail trail that specifies the S3 bucket as the storage location.
C. Configure the EventBridge rule to use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue as a dead-letter queue.
D. Configure the EventBridge rule to use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue as a dead-letter queue.
E. Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs Specify the log group as an additional target of the EventBridge rule.
questions.explanation: Amazon EventBridge can send matching events to an additional CloudWatch Logs target so testers can inspect the event payloads. AWS CloudTrail records AWS API activity and delivers log files to the configured Amazon S3 bucket, providing an audit record for troubleshooting. An EventBridge target dead-letter queue retains undeliverable events for later analysis or processing; EventBridge supports only standard Amazon SQS queues as rule DLQs, not FIFO queues.
learnMore: Using dead-letter queues to process undelivered events in EventBridge
Event bus targets in Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to administer its AWS accounts. The company has a root OU with a child OU. The root OU has an SCP that permits all actions on all resources. The child OU has an SCP that permits all Amazon DynamoDB and AWS Lambda actions and denies every other action. The company has an AWS account named vendor-data in the child OU. A DevOps engineer has an IAM user with the Administrator Access IAM policy attached in the vendor-data account. The DevOps engineer tries to launch an Amazon EC2 instance in the vendor-data account but receives an access denied error. Which change should the DevOps engineer make to launch the EC2 instance in the vendor-data account?
options: A. Attach the AmazonEC2FullAccess IAM policy to the IAM user.
B. Create a new SCP that allows all actions for Amazon EC2. Attach the SCP to the vendor-data account.
C. Update the SCP in the child OU to allow all actions for Amazon EC2.
D. Create a new SCP that allows all actions for Amazon EC2. Attach the SCP to the root OU.
questions.explanation: The child OU SCP explicitly denies Amazon EC2 actions, so it limits the IAM user's AdministratorAccess permissions. Explicit SCP denies take precedence over allows attached at lower levels, including an SCP on the account. Updating the child OU SCP to allow Amazon EC2 actions removes the applicable restriction while the root OU and IAM policy already allow the action.
learnMore: SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations
Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. At startup, the application must process data from an Amazon S3 bucket before it can begin serving requests. The amount of data stored in the S3 bucket is increasing. When the Auto Scaling group adds instances, the application now needs several minutes to download and process the data before it can serve requests. The company must reduce the elapsed time before new EC2 instances are ready to serve requests. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to reduce application startup time?
options: A. Configure a warm pool for the Auto Scaling group with warmed EC2 instances in the Stopped state. Configure an autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING lifecycle hook on the Auto Scaling group. Modify the application to complete the lifecycle hook when the application is ready to serve requests.

B. Increase the maximum instance count of the Auto Scaling group. Configure an autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING lifecycle hook on the Auto Scaling group. Modify the application to complete the lifecycle hook when the application is ready to serve requests.

C. Configure a warm pool for the Auto Scaling group with warmed EC2 instances in the Running state. Configure an autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING lifecycle hook on the Auto Scaling group. Modify the application to complete the lifecycle hook when the application is ready to serve requests.

D. Increase the maximum instance count of the Auto Scaling group. Configure an autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING lifecycle hook on the Auto Scaling group. Modify the application to complete the lifecycle hook and to place the new instance in the Standby state when the application is ready to serve requests.
questions.explanation: An EC2 Auto Scaling warm pool supplies pre-initialized instances during scale-out. A launch lifecycle hook keeps an instance out of service until its initialization, including the S3 data download and processing, is complete. A Stopped warm-pool state minimizes cost because EC2 instance charges do not apply while the instance is stopped, while the prepared EBS volumes are retained. AWS documents that stopped warm-pool instances are an effective way to minimize costs and that lifecycle hooks ensure initialization finishes before an instance is put into service.
learnMore: Decrease latency for applications with long boot times using warm pools
Use lifecycle hooks with a warm pool in Auto Scaling groups

questions.questionText: A company builds container images and stores them in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) in the company’s primary AWS Region. A DevOps engineer needs to replicate all of the company’s ECR repository images to a secondary Region. The engineer creates a new ECR repository in the secondary Region and configures permissions on that repository to permit replication. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Pull the existing primary ECR images and then push the images to the secondary ECR repository. Create a replication rule on the primary ECR registry to replicate the images to the secondary ECR registry.
B. Pull the existing primary ECR images and then push the images to the secondary ECR repository. Configure permission on the primary ECR registry to allow access from the secondary Region.

C. Configure permission on the primary ECR registry to allow access from the secondary Region. Create a replication rule on the primary ECR registry to replicate the images to the secondary ECR registry.

D. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automatically save the ECR images to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure cross-Region replication for the S3 bucket. Configure a second Lambda function to push the images to ECR repositories in the replication destination Region when images are replicated to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR replication is configured on the source registry and provides ongoing cross-Region replication for images after the replication configuration is enabled. It does not replicate repository content that already existed before configuration, so those existing images require a one-time pull from the primary repository and push to the secondary repository. A source-registry replication rule then handles future images without custom automation.
learnMore: Private image replication in Amazon ECR
Configuring private image replication in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A company manually provisions IAM access for its employees and wants to replace that manual process with an automated one. The company has an existing Active Directory system configured with an external SAML 2.0 identity provider (IdP). The company wants employees to use their existing corporate credentials to access AWS. Groups from the existing Active Directory system must be available for permission management in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). A DevOps engineer has completed the initial configuration of AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the company’s AWS account. What should the DevOps engineer do next to fulfill the requirements?
options: A. Configure an external IdP as an identity source. Configure automatic provisioning of users and groups by using the SCIM protocol.
B. Configure AWS Directory Service as an identity source. Configure automatic provisioning of users and groups by using the SAML protocol.
C. Configure an AD Connector as an identity source. Configure automatic provisioning of users and groups by using the SCIM protocol.
D. Configure an external IdP as an identity source Configure automatic provisioning of users and groups by using the SAML protocol.
questions.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center supports external identity providers through SAML 2.0 for user authentication, allowing employees to sign in with corporate credentials. Because SAML does not provide user and group synchronization, users and groups must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center; SCIM v2.0 provides the automatic provisioning required for group-based permission management.
learnMore: External identity providers - AWS IAM Identity Center

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must configure a blue/green deployment for an existing three-tier application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon RDS database. The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and are in an Auto Scaling group. The DevOps engineer has created launch templates, Auto Scaling groups, and ALB target groups for both the blue and green environments. Each target group specifies which application version—blue or green—will be loaded on the EC2 instances. An Amazon Route 53 record for www.example.com points to the ALB. The deployment must move traffic all at once from the blue environment to the green environment. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Starta rolling restart of the Auto Scaling group for the green environment to deploy the new application version to the green environment's EC2 instances. When the rolling restart is complete, use an AWS CLI command to update the ALB to send traffic to the green environment's target group.

B. Use an AWS CLI command to update the ALB to send traffic to the green environments target group. Start a rolling restart of the Auto Scaling group for the green environment to deploy the new application version to the green environment's EC2 instances.

C. Update the launch template to deploy the green environment's application version to the blue environment's EC2 instances. Do not change the target groups or the Auto Scaling groups in either environment. Perform a rolling restart of the blue environments EC2 instances.

D. Starta rolling restart of the Auto Scaling group for the green environment to deploy the new application version to the green environment's EC2 instances. When the rolling restart is complete, update Route 53 to point to the green environment's endpoint on the ALB.
questions.explanation: The green Auto Scaling group must be refreshed before cutover so its instances are running the green version. Updating the ALB listener’s forward action to the green target group directs new requests to that prepared environment in a single load-balancer routing change. The Route 53 record already points to the ALB, so DNS does not need to change.
learnMore: Edit a listener rule for your Application Load Balancer

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer uses AWS WAF to administer web ACLs throughout an AWS account. The DevOps engineer must make sure that AWS WAF is enabled on every Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the account. The DevOps engineer uses an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a separate ALB and AWS WAF as part of each application stack’s deployment process. If AWS WAF is removed from an ALB after that ALB has been deployed, AWS WAF must be automatically added back to the ALB. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Enable AWS Config. Add the alb-waf-enabled managed rule. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to add AWS WAF to an ALB. Edit the rule to automatically remediate. Select the Systems Manager Automation document as the remediation action.

B. Enable AWS Config. Add the alb-waf-enabled managed rule. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to send all AWS Config ConfigurationItemChangeNotification notification types to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to call the AWS Config start-resource-evaluation API in detective mode.

C. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to periodically call an AWS Lambda function that calls the detect-stack-drift API on the CloudFormation template. Configure the Lambda function to modify the ALB attributes with waf.fail_open.enabled set to true if the AWS::WAFv2::WebACLAssociation resource shows a status of drifted.

D. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to periodically call an AWS Lambda function that calls the detect-stack-drift API on the CloudFormation template. Configure the Lambda function to delete and redeploy the CloudFormation stack if the AWS::WAFv2::WebACLAssociation resource shows a status of drifted.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule ALB_WAF_ENABLED detects an ALB without an associated AWS WAF web ACL on configuration changes. AWS Config can automatically remediate a noncompliant resource by running a Systems Manager Automation document, which can associate the required web ACL with the affected ALB. This provides event-driven detection and remediation without custom Lambda functions, periodic drift checks, or stack redeployment.
learnMore: alb-waf-enabled - AWS Config
Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config
