questions.questionText: A company runs an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster to deploy its web applications in containers. The web applications include confidential data that cannot be decrypted without particular credentials. A DevOps engineer stored the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. The secrets are encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. A Kubernetes service account for a third-party tool exposes the secrets to the applications. The service account assumes a company-created IAM role to access the secrets. The service account gets an Access Denied (403 Forbidden) error when it attempts to retrieve the secrets from Secrets Manager. What is the root cause of this issue?
options: A. The IAM role that is attached to the EKS cluster does not have access to retrieve the secrets from Secrets Manager.
B. The key policy for the customer managed key does not allow the Kubernetes service account IAM role to use the key.
C. The key policy for the customer managed key does not allow the EKS cluster IAM role to use the key.
D. The IAM role that is assumed by the Kubernetes service account does not have permission to access the EKS cluster.
questions.explanation: For a secret encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, GetSecretValue also requires kms:Decrypt permission on that key. Secrets Manager performs the KMS decryption on behalf of the IAM principal requesting the secret, so the Kubernetes service account’s assumed IAM role must be authorized to use the customer managed key. The EKS cluster IAM role is not the requesting principal.
learnMore: GetSecretValue - AWS Secrets Manager API Reference
Secret encryption and decryption in AWS Secrets Manager

questions.questionText: A company has a newly created AWS account that teams will use to deploy various applications. The teams will create many Amazon S3 buckets for application-specific use and for storing AWS CloudTrail logs. The company has enabled Amazon Macie for the account. A DevOps engineer must optimize Amazon Macie costs for the account without compromising the account’s functionality. Which solutions meet these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Exclude S3 buckets that contain CloudTrail logs from automated discovery.
B. Exclude S3 buckets that have public read access from automated discovery.
C. Configure scheduled daily discovery jobs for all S3 buckets in the account.
D. Configure discovery jobs to include S3 objects based on the last modified criterion.
E. Configure discovery jobs to include S3 objects that are tagged as production only.
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie supports excluding selected S3 buckets from automated sensitive data discovery, and AWS specifically cites buckets that store AWS CloudTrail event logs as suitable exclusions. Sensitive data discovery jobs also support a Last modified object criterion, which limits the objects analyzed to a specified time period and reduces the amount of data processed. Excluding publicly readable buckets or limiting analysis only to production-tagged objects can omit sensitive data from scope.
learnMore: Configuring settings for automated sensitive data discovery - Amazon Macie
Scope options for sensitive data discovery jobs - Amazon Macie

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must implement a CI/CD pipeline in an AWS account. The pipeline must use sensitive database credentials stored in an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter. The Parameter Store parameter resides in a separate central account. The DevOps engineer must create and integrate the parameter with the CI/CD account. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Use an advanced tier Parameter Store parameter to store the database credentials in the central AWS account.
B. Create an IAM role in the AWS account that hosts the CI/CD pipeline. Add the full ARN of the parameter to the IAM policy that is associated with the IAM role.
C. Use a standard tier Parameter Store parameter to store the database credentials in the central AWS account.
D. Use an AWS KMS managed key to encrypt the parameter. Grant decrypt permissions for the KMS key to the AWS account that hosts the CI/CD pipeline.
E. Use a customer managed AWS KMS key to encrypt the parameter. Grant decrypt permissions for the customer managed key to the AWS account that hosts the CI/CD pipeline.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store supports cross-account sharing only for advanced-tier parameters. A shared SecureString parameter must be encrypted with a customer managed AWS KMS key, because AWS managed keys cannot be shared across accounts. The parameter is shared with the CI/CD account through an AWS RAM resource share, which grants the consumer account read access to the shared parameter.
learnMore: Working with shared parameters in Parameter Store
Managing tiers for Parameter Store parameters

questions.questionText: During a security audit, a company found that some security groups permit SSH traffic from 0.0.0.0/0. A security team must implement a solution to detect and remediate this issue as quickly as possible. The company uses a single organization in AWS Organizations to manage all of the company's AWS accounts. Which solution will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Enable AWS Config for all AWS accounts. Use a periodic trigger to activate the vpe-sg-port-restriction-check AWS Config rule. Create an AWS Lambda function to remediate any noncompliant rules.

B. Create an AWS Lambda function in each AWS account to delete all the security group rules. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match security group update events or creation events. Set the Lambda function in each account as a target for the rule.

C. Enable AWS Config for all AWS accounts. Create a custom AWS Config rule to run on the restricted-ssh configuration change trigger. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to remediate any noncompliant resources.

D. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation document in each account to inspect all security groups and to delete noncompliant rules. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Automation document every hour.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule restricted-ssh identifies security groups as noncompliant when inbound SSH is open to 0.0.0.0/0 (or ::/0). A configuration-change trigger evaluates a matching resource whenever its configuration changes, allowing an AWS Lambda-based process to remediate the noncompliant security-group rule promptly.
learnMore: restricted-ssh - AWS Config
Creating AWS Config Custom Lambda Rules

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer at a company supports an AWS environment where all users use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). The company wants to immediately disable the credentials of every newly created IAM user and notify the security team. Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to an IAM CreateUser API call in AWS CloudTrail.
B. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to an IAM GetLoginProfile API call in AWS CloudTrail.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Configure the Lambda function to disable any access keys and delete the login profiles that are associated with the IAM user.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Configure the Lambda function to delete the login profiles that are associated with the IAM user.
E. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Subscribe the security team's group email address to the topic.
questions.explanation: IAM API events delivered through CloudTrail can be matched by an EventBridge rule, including a CreateUser event. A Lambda function can disable IAM access keys and delete the IAM user's login profile; deleting only the login profile does not prevent API access through active keys. An EventBridge rule can also target an Amazon SNS topic, whose email subscription notifies the security team's group address.
learnMore: DeleteLoginProfile - AWS Identity and Access Management

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer at a company supports an AWS environment where all users use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). The company wants to immediately disable the credentials of every newly created IAM user and notify the security team. Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to an IAM CreateUser API call in AWS CloudTrail.
B. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to an IAM GetLoginProfile API call in AWS CloudTrail.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Configure the Lambda function to disable any access keys and delete the login profiles that are associated with the IAM user.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Configure the Lambda function to delete the login profiles that are associated with the IAM user.
E. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that is a target of the EventBridge rule. Subscribe the security team's group email address to the topic.
questions.explanation: IAM API events delivered through CloudTrail can be matched by an EventBridge rule, including a CreateUser event. A Lambda function can disable IAM access keys and delete the IAM user's login profile; deleting only the login profile does not prevent API access through active keys. An EventBridge rule can also target an Amazon SNS topic, whose email subscription notifies the security team's group address.
learnMore: DeleteLoginProfile - AWS Identity and Access Management

questions.questionText: A development team manually builds an artifact locally and then stores it in an Amazon S3 bucket. The application has a local cache that must be cleared whenever a deployment takes place. The team runs a command to perform this task, downloads the artifact from Amazon S3, and unzips it to finish the deployment. A DevOps team wants to move to a CI/CD process and include checks that stop and roll back the deployment if a failure occurs. The team must track the deployment's progression. Which combination of actions will achieve this? Choose three
options: A. Allow developers to check the code into a code repository. Using Amazon EventBridge, on every pull into the main branch, invoke an AWS Lambda function to build the artifact and store it in Amazon S3.
B. Create a custom script to clear the cache. Specify the script in the BeforeInstall lifecycle hook in the AppSpec file.
C. Create user data for each Amazon EC2 instance that contains the clear cache script. Once deployed, test the application. If it is not successful, deploy it again.
D. Set up AWS CodePipeline to deploy the application. Allow developers to check the code into a code repository as a source for the pipeline.
E. Use AWS CodeBuild to build the artifact and place it in Amazon S3. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the artifact to Amazon EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: AWS CodePipeline provides the CI/CD orchestration and tracks the progression of source, build, and deployment stages. AWS CodeBuild can build the application artifact, and AWS CodeDeploy can deploy that revision to Amazon EC2 instances and report lifecycle-hook failures for deployment control and rollback. For EC2 deployments, an AppSpec file can associate scripts with lifecycle events; BeforeInstall is intended for preinstallation tasks, making it suitable for the cache-clearing script.
learnMore: AppSpec 'hooks' section - AWS CodeDeploy
Use AWS CodeBuild with AWS CodePipeline to test code and run builds

questions.questionText: A company has enabled all features in its AWS Organizations organization. The organization has 10 AWS accounts. The company has enabled AWS CloudTrail in every account. The company expects the number of AWS accounts in the organization to grow to 500 over the next year. The company plans to use multiple OUs for these accounts. The company has enabled AWS Config in each current AWS account in the organization. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that automatically enables AWS Config for all future AWS accounts created in the organization. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. In the organization's management account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to a CreateAccount API call. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that enables trusted access to AWS Config for the organization.

B. In the organization's management account, create an AWS CloudFormation stack set to enable AWS Config. Configure the stack set to deploy automatically when an account is created through Organizations.
C. In the organization's management account, create an SCP that allows the appropriate AWS Config API calls to enable AWS Config. Apply the SCP to the root-level OU.

D. In the organization's management account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to a CreateAccount API call. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to enable AWS Config for the account.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation StackSets using service-managed permissions can target an organization or OUs and automatically deploy stack instances when new AWS accounts are added. A StackSet that contains the AWS Config resources therefore enables AWS Config consistently in future accounts at organizational scale.
learnMore: Enable or disable automatic deployments for StackSets in AWS Organizations
Get started with StackSets using a sample template

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must back up sensitive Amazon S3 objects stored in an S3 bucket that has a private bucket policy by using S3 cross-Region replication. The objects must be copied to a target bucket in another AWS Region and AWS account. Which combination of actions should be taken to enable this replication? Choose three
options: A. Create a replication IAM role in the source account
B. Create a replication I AM role in the target account.
C. Add statements to the source bucket policy allowing the replication IAM role to replicate objects.
D. Add statements to the target bucket policy allowing the replication IAM role to replicate objects.
E. Create a replication rule in the source bucket to enable the replication.
questions.explanation: Cross-account Amazon S3 replication requires a replication IAM role that Amazon S3 can assume, a replication rule configured on the source bucket, and a destination-bucket policy granting the source-account replication role permission to replicate objects. A private source-bucket policy must also allow that role to read the source objects unless its existing policy already provides that access. Because the stated requirement is to choose three while also describing a private source policy, the choices are ambiguous: A, D, and E are the core setup actions, while C may additionally be necessary depending on the existing source policy.
learnMore: Setting up permissions for live replication
Configuring replication for buckets in different accounts

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Recently, an issue prevented EC2 instances from launching successfully, and the support team took several hours to identify it. The support team wants email notification whenever an EC2 instance fails to start successfully. Which action will achieve this?
options: A. Add a health check to the Auto Scaling group to invoke an AWS Lambda function whenever an instance status is impaired.
B. Configure the Auto Scaling group to send a notification to an Amazon SNS topic whenever a failed instance launch occurs.
C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that invokes an AWS Lambda function when a failed AttachInstances Auto Scaling API call is made.
D. Create a status check alarm on Amazon EC2 to send a notification to an Amazon SNS topic whenever a status check fail occurs.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can publish an Amazon SNS notification for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR event when an instance launch fails. Subscribing an email endpoint to that SNS topic sends the support team the required notification. Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application needs frequent restarts. Its logs contain error messages whenever a restart is needed, and the logs are published to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. An Amazon CloudWatch alarm notifies an application engineer through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the logs contain a high number of restart-related error messages. After receiving an SNS-topic notification, the application engineer manually restarts the application on the instances. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that automates restarting the application on the instances without restarting the instances. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Configure an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that runs a script to restart the application on the instances. Configure the SNS topic to invoke the runbook.
B. Create an AWS Lambda function that restarts the application on the instances. Configure the Lambda function as an event destination of the SNS topic.

C. Configure an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that runs a script to restart the application on the instances. Create an AWS Lambda function to invoke the runbook. Configure the Lambda function as an event destination of the SNS topic.

D. Configure an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that runs a script to restart the application on the instances. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when the CloudWatch alarm enters ALARM state. Specify the runbook as a target of the rule.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch sends alarm state-change events directly to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can match an alarm entering the ALARM state and directly target an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook, which can run a restart script on the managed EC2 instances. This provides event-driven remediation without an additional Lambda function or an SNS-mediated invocation path. Amazon CloudWatch events Run automations based on EventBridge events
learnMore: Run automations based on EventBridge events - AWS Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must add integration tests to an existing AWS CodePipeline CI/CD workflow for an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service. The CI/CD workflow retrieves new application code from an AWS CodeCommit repository and builds a container image. It then uploads the container image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) using a new image-tag version. The integration tests must verify that new versions of the service endpoint are reachable and that various API methods return successful response data. The DevOps engineer has already created an ECS cluster for testing the service. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the LEAST management overhead? Choose three
options: A. Add a deploy stage to the pipeline. Configure Amazon ECS as the action provider.
B. Add a deploy stage to the pipeline. Configure AWS CodeDeploy as the action provider.
C. Add an appspec.yml file to the CodeCommit repository.
D. Update the image build pipeline stage to output an imagedefinitions.json file that references the new image tag.
E. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs connectivity checks and API calls against the service. Integrate the Lambda function with CodePipeline by using a Lambda action stage.
questions.explanation: The Amazon ECS standard deploy action deploys the new image to the ECS service and requires an imagedefinitions.json input that identifies the container and new ECR image tag. A Lambda action can run the connectivity checks and API calls as a serverless pipeline step, avoiding managed test infrastructure. AWS CodeDeploy and an AppSpec file are required for the more involved ECS blue/green deployment workflow, not for a standard ECS deployment.
learnMore: Image definitions file reference

questions.questionText: A company launches a new application in a new AWS account. The application contains an AWS Lambda function that processes messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. The Lambda function saves the results to an Amazon S3 bucket for additional downstream processing. The Lambda function must process messages within a specified time period after the messages are published. The Lambda function uses a batch size of 10 messages and takes a few seconds to process each batch. As load rises on the application's first day of operation, queue messages accumulate faster than the Lambda function can process them. Some messages fail to meet the required processing timelines. Logs indicate that many queued messages contain invalid data. The company must meet the timeline requirements for messages with valid data. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Increase the Lambda function's batch size. Change the SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue. Request a Lambda concurrency increase in the AWS Region.
B. Reduce the Lambda function's batch size. Increase the SQS message throughput quota. Request a Lambda concurrency increase in the AWS Region.
C. Increase the Lambda function's batch size. Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket. Configure an SQS dead-letter queue.
D. Keep the Lambda function's batch size the same. Configure the Lambda function to report failed batch items. Configure an SQS dead-letter queue.
questions.explanation: For an Amazon SQS event source, a failure in one record normally causes Lambda to return the entire batch to the queue, so valid records can be repeatedly retried alongside invalid records. Configuring ReportBatchItemFailures lets the function report only the failed records, allowing successfully processed valid records to remain complete. An SQS dead-letter queue removes repeatedly failing invalid messages after the configured maximum receives, preventing poison messages from consuming processing capacity and delaying valid messages. Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda and Benefits of using partial batch responses for Amazon SQS event sources.
learnMore: Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda
Benefits of using partial batch responses for Amazon SQS event sources

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must apply a core set of security controls to an existing collection of AWS accounts. The accounts belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. Individual teams will administer their individual accounts by using the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy. For all accounts, AWS CloudTrail and AWS Config must be enabled in every available AWS Region. Individual account administrators must not be able to modify or delete any baseline resources. However, those administrators must be able to modify or delete their own CloudTrail trails and AWS Config rules. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that defines the standard account resources. Deploy the template to all accounts from the organization's management account by using CloudFormation StackSets. Set the stack policy to deny Update:Delete actions.
B. Enable AWS Control Tower. Enroll the existing accounts in AWS Control Tower. Grant the individual account administrators access to CloudTrail and AWS Config.

C. Designate an AWS Config management account. Create AWS Config recorders in all accounts by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Deploy AWS Config rules to the organization by using the AWS Config management account. Create a CloudTrail organization trail in the organization’s management account. Deny modification or deletion of the AWS Config recorders by using an SCP.

D. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that defines the standard account resources. Deploy the template to all accounts from the organization's management account by using Cloud Formation StackSets Create an SCP that prevents updates or deletions to CloudTrail resources or AWS Config resources unless the principal is an administrator of the organization's management account.
questions.explanation: An AWS CloudTrail organization trail provides centralized, multi-Region logging across member accounts, and member-account users cannot modify or delete that trail. AWS Config organization rules are centrally administered from the AWS Config management or delegated administrator account. Deploying configuration recorders through StackSets and using an SCP only to deny changes to those baseline recorders protects the required Config collection while leaving account administrators able to create, modify, and delete their own CloudTrail trails and AWS Config rules.
learnMore: Creating a trail for an organization - AWS CloudTrail
delete-organization-config-rule - AWS CLI Command Reference

questions.questionText: A company makes proprietary data available through an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company must ensure that only users at the corporate office, with a known set of IP address ranges, can access the distribution. An AWS WAF web ACL is associated with the distribution and its default action is set to Count. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a new regex pattern set. Add the regex pattern set to a new rule group. Create a new web ACL that has a default action set to Block. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. Add a rule that allows traffic based on the new rule group.

B. Create an AWS WAF IP address set that matches the corporate office IP address range. Create a new web ACL that has a default action set to Allow. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. Add a rule that allows traffic from the IP address set.

C. Create a new regex pattern set. Add the regex pattern set to a new rule group. Set the default action on the existing web ACL to Allow. Add a rule that has priority 0 that allows traffic based on the regex pattern set.

D. Create a WAF IP address set that matches the corporate office IP address range. Set the default action on the existing web ACL to Block. Add a rule that has priority 0 that allows traffic from the IP address set.
questions.explanation: An AWS WAF IP set directly identifies the corporate office CIDR ranges. Setting the existing web ACL’s default action to Block and adding an Allow rule for that IP set permits only matching corporate-office requests; every request that does not match the allow rule is blocked. This reuses the existing web ACL and avoids unnecessary regex pattern sets, rule groups, and a replacement ACL.
learnMore: Setting the protection pack (web ACL) default action in AWS WAF
WebACL - AWS WAFV2 API Reference

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must troubleshoot a pipeline that uses a GitHub code repository. The pipeline includes a source stage, a build stage, and a deploy stage. It also has an AWS CodeStar connection to the GitHub code repository. The build stage uses an AWS CodeBuild build project. As part of the build process, the build project must perform a git clone of the repository. The DevOps engineer confirms that the source stage works correctly. However, the build stage fails whenever the pipeline runs. What causes the build stage to fail in the pipeline?
options: A. The build stage within the pipeline needs to use the AWS CodeStar connection action.
B. The AWS CodeStar connection to GitHub contains incorrect credentials.
C. The AWS CodePipeline service role does not have permission to use the AWS CodeStar connection.
D. The AWS CodeBuild service role does not have permission to use the AWS CodeStar connection.
questions.explanation: When a CodePipeline GitHub source action supplies a full Git clone reference to a downstream CodeBuild action, the CodeBuild project service role must be allowed to use the connection. Grant codestar-connections:UseConnection on the connection ARN to that role; otherwise, CodeBuild cannot clone the repository even if the source stage succeeds.
learnMore: Tutorial: Use full clone with a GitHub pipeline source

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is building an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a web service. The web service will run on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The DevOps engineer must ensure that the service can receive requests from clients with IPv6 addresses. What should the DevOps engineer do in the CloudFormation template to allow IPv6 clients to access the web service?
options: A. Add an IPv6 CIDR block to the VPC and the private subnet for the EC2 instances. Create route table entries for the IPv6 network, use EC2 instance types that support IPv6, and assign IPv6 addresses to each EC2 instance.

B. Assign each EC2 instance an IPv6 Elastic IP address. Create a target group, and add the EC2 instances as targets. Create a listener on port 443 of the ALB, and associate the target group with the ALB.
C. Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Add an IPv6 CIDR block to the VPC and subnets for the NLB, and assign the NLB an IPv6 Elastic IP address.

D. Add an IPv6 CIDR block to the VPC and subnets for the ALB. Create a listener on port 443. and specify the dualstack IP address type on the ALB. Create a target group, and add the EC2 instances as targets. Associate the target group with the ALB.
questions.explanation: A dualstack Application Load Balancer accepts both IPv4 and IPv6 client connections and publishes an AAAA DNS record for IPv6 clients. The VPC and subnets selected for the ALB must have IPv6 CIDR blocks. The ALB can still route requests to EC2 targets by using an IPv4 target group, so the private EC2 instances do not need IPv6 addresses solely to support IPv6 clients.
learnMore: Application Load Balancers – Elastic Load Balancing
Create an Application Load Balancer

questions.questionText: A company recently set up AWS Control Tower in its AWS Organizations organization. The company enrolled all existing AWS accounts in AWS Control Tower. It wants to make sure that every new AWS account is automatically enrolled in AWS Control Tower. The company already has an AWS Step Functions workflow that creates new AWS accounts and carries out any actions required during account creation. The Step Functions workflow is defined in the same AWS account as AWS Control Tower. Which combination of steps should the company add to the Step Functions workflow to meet these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge event that has an aws.controltower source and a CreateManagedAccount detail-type. Add the details of the new AWS account to the detail field of the event.
B. Create an Amazon EventBridge event that has an aws.controltower source and a SetupLandingZone detail-type. Add the details of the new AWS account to the detail field of the event.
C. Create an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the new AWS account. Configure the role to allow the AWS Control Tower administrator account to assume the role.
D. Call the AWS Service Catalog ProvisionProduct API operation with the details of the new AWS account.
E. Call the Organizations EnableAWSServiceAccess API operation with the controltower.amazonaws.com service name and the details of the new AWS account.
questions.explanation: An account created outside Account Factory must have the AWSControlTowerExecution role, with a trust relationship that allows the AWS Control Tower administrator account to assume it, before it can be enrolled. AWS Control Tower supports automated enrollment of an existing member account through the AWS Service Catalog ProvisionProduct API; that API starts the Account Factory enrollment/provisioning workflow.
learnMore: Automate Account Provisioning in AWS Control Tower by Service Catalog APIs
Prerequisites for enrollment

questions.questionText: A company has an AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled, AWS CloudTrail trusted access configured for the management account, and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic configured for notifications. The company requires all AWS events across every AWS Region in the organization to be recorded and retained in an audit account. It also requires near-real-time notifications for any failed login attempts. A DevOps engineer has created an organization trail in the management account to log events in all Regions. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the audit account. In the audit account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to failed login events in CloudTrail. Configure the EventBridge rule to notify the SNS topic.

B. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the management account. Configure an Amazon Athena table to read from the new S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that queries the Athena table for failed login events and publishes the findings to the SNS topic. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes.

C. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the audit account and a new Amazon CloudWatch log group in the management account. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the log group to create a custom metric for failed logins. Configure a CloudWatch alarm that uses the custom metric and notifies the SNS topic.

D. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon CloudWatch log group in the audit account. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream in the audit account. Configure a subscription filter on the log group to send the logs to the data stream. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to filter the data stream for failed logins. Publish the results to the SNS topic.
questions.explanation: An organization trail can centrally log activity from all organization accounts and enabled Regions. CloudTrail log files can be delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket in a different AWS account, allowing retention in the audit account. For an organization trail, the CloudWatch Logs log group must be in the current management account. A CloudWatch Logs metric filter can identify failed-login events, and a CloudWatch alarm can publish to the configured SNS topic with near-real-time notification.
learnMore: Creating a trail for your organization in the console - AWS CloudTrail
Creating a trail for an organization - AWS CloudTrail

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is developing a solution that uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues. The solution also contains an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. The Lambda function retrieves content from an SQS queue event source and writes that content to the DynamoDB table. The solution must maximize Lambda scalability and prevent successfully processed SQS messages from being processed more than once. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Decrease the batch window to 1 second when configuring the Lambda function's event source mapping.
B. Decrease the batch size to 1 when configuring the Lambda function's event source mapping.
C. Include the ReportBatchItemFailures value in the FunctionResponseTypes list in the Lambda function's event source mapping.
D. Set the queue visibility timeout on the Lambda function's event source mapping to account for invocation throttling of the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Configuring ReportBatchItemFailures in FunctionResponseTypes enables partial batch responses for an SQS event source mapping. Lambda can retry only the failed messages rather than making successfully processed messages in the same batch visible again. With partial batch responses enabled, Lambda does not reduce message polling when invocations fail, preserving processing scalability.
learnMore: Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda
Using Lambda with Amazon SQS

questions.questionText: A company has containerized all of its internally developed quality-control applications. It runs Jenkins on Amazon EC2 instances that need patching and upgrades. Because build artifacts contain company intellectual property, the compliance officer has asked a DevOps engineer to begin encrypting them. What should the DevOps engineer do to achieve this in the MOST maintainable way?
options: A. Automate patching and upgrading using AWS Systems Manager on EC2 instances and encrypt Amazon EBS volumes by default.
B. Deploy Jenkins to an Amazon ECS cluster and copy build artifacts to an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled.
C. Leverage AWS CodePipeline with a build action and encrypt the artifacts using AWS Secrets Manager.
D. Use AWS CodeBuild with artifact encryption to replace the Jenkins instance running on EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed build service that eliminates maintenance of Jenkins EC2 hosts. Its build artifacts are encrypted at rest by default with AWS KMS, and a customer-managed KMS key can be configured when required. AWS Secrets Manager is intended for storing and retrieving secrets, not as the primary build-artifact encryption service.

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company is moving from its on-premises data center to AWS. Question 130 / Configuration Management and IaC A company is moving from its on-premises data center to AWS. It currently uses a custom on-premises CI/CD pipeline solution to build and package software. The company wants its software packages and dependent public repositories to be available in AWS CodeArtifact to support creation of application-specific pipelines. Which combination of steps should the company take to update the CI/CD pipeline solution and configure CodeArtifact with the LEAST operational overhead? Choose two
options: A. Update the C1ICD pipeline to create a VM image that contains newly packaged software. Use AWS Import/Export to make the VM image available as an Amazon EC2 AMI. Launch the AMI with an attached IAM instance profile that allows CodeArtifact actions. Use AWS CLI commands to publish the packages to a CodeArtifact repository.

B. Create an AWS Identity and Access Management Roles Anywhere trust anchor. Create an IAM role that allows CodeArtifact actions and that has a trust relationship on the trust anchor. Update the on-premises CI/CD pipeline to assume the new IAM role and to publish the packages to CodeArtifact.

C. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket. Generate a presigned URL that allows the PutObject request. Update the on-premises CI/CD pipeline to use the presigned URL to publish the packages from the on-premises location to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when packages are created in the bucket through a put command. Configure the Lambda function to publish the packages to CodeArtifact.
D. For each public repository, create a CodeArutact repository that is configured with an external connection. Configure the dependent repositories as upstream public repositories.
E. Create a Codeartitact repository that is configured with a set of external connections to the public repositories. Configure the external connections to be downstream of the repository.
questions.explanation: IAM Roles Anywhere lets workloads outside AWS obtain temporary IAM credentials through a trust anchor and an IAM role, so an on-premises CI/CD pipeline can publish packages to CodeArtifact without managing long-term AWS credentials or additional compute and transfer components. CodeArtifact supports only one external connection per repository; the recommended design is one repository with an external connection for each public repository and to configure dependent repositories to use those repositories as upstreams.

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company application uses a fleet of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances to analyze and process data. Question 131 / Resilient Cloud Solutions A company application uses a fleet of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances to analyze and process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group. The Auto Scaling group is a target group for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application analyzes critical data that cannot tolerate interruption. It also analyzes noncritical data that can tolerate interruption. The critical-data analysis needs to scale quickly in response to real-time application demand. The noncritical-data analysis consumes memory. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that decreases scale-out latency for the critical data. The solution must also process the noncritical data. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. For the critical data, modify the existing Auto Scaling group. Create a warm pool instance in the stopped state. Define the warm pool size. Create a new version of the launch template that has detailed monitoring enabled. Use Spot Instances.

B. For the critical data, modify the existing Auto Scaling group. Create a warm pool instance in the stopped state. Define the warm pool size. Create a new version of the launch template that has detailed monitoring enabled. Use On-Demand Instances.

C. For the critical data, modify the existing Auto Scaling group. Create a lifecycle hook to ensure that bootstrap scripts are completed successfully. Ensure that the application on the instances is ready to accept traffic before the instances are registered. Create a new version of the launch template that has detailed monitoring enabled.

D. For the noncritical data, create a second Auto Scaling group that uses a launch template. Configure the launch template to install the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent and to configure the CloudWatch agent with a custom memory utilization metric. Use Spot Instances. Add the new Auto Scaling group as the target group for the ALB. Modify the application to use two target groups for critical data and noncritical data.

E. For the noncritical data, create a second Auto Scaling group. Choose the predefined memory utilization metric type for the target tracking scaling policy. Use Spot Instances. Add the new Auto Scaling group as the target group for the ALB. Modify the application to use two target groups for critical data and noncritical data.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools keep pre-initialized instances available for faster scale-out. A stopped warm pool with On-Demand Instances is appropriate for critical processing because warm pools do not support Spot Instances in mixed instance groups and the workload cannot tolerate interruption. Memory utilization is not an EC2 Auto Scaling predefined target-tracking metric, so the noncritical workload requires the CloudWatch agent to publish a custom memory-utilization metric; Spot Instances are appropriate because that processing can withstand interruption.
learnMore: Decrease latency for applications with long boot times using warm pools

questions.questionText: An application running on a group of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group needs a configuration file to run. The instances are created and managed by AWS CloudFormation. A DevOps engineer wants instances to receive the most recent configuration file at launch, and wants configuration-file changes to appear on all instances with minimal delay when the CloudFormation template is updated. Company policy requires application configuration files to be kept in source control together with AWS infrastructure configuration files. Which solution will achieve this?
options: A. In the CloudFormation template, add an AWS Config rule. Place the configuration file content in the rule’s InputParameters property, and set the Scope property to the EC2 Auto Scaling group. Add an AWS Systems Manager Resource Data Sync resource to the template to poll for updates to the configuration.

B. In the CloudFormation template, add an EC2 launch template resource. Place the configuration file content in the launch template. Configure the cfn-init script to run when the instance is launched, and configure the cfn-hup script to poll for updates to the configuration.

C. In the CloudFormation template, add an EC2 launch template resource. Place the configuration file content in the launch template. Add an AWS Systems Manager Resource Data Sync resource to the template to poll for updates to the configuration.

D. In the CloudFormation template, add CloudFormation init metadata. Place the configuration file content in the metadata. Configure the cfn-init script to run when the instance is launched, and configure the cfn-hup script to poll for updates to the configuration.
questions.explanation: AWS::CloudFormation::Init metadata can define files for EC2 instances, and cfn-init retrieves that metadata and writes the files during instance initialization. The cfn-hup daemon detects changes to CloudFormation resource metadata and runs a configured hook, commonly re-running cfn-init, so updates to the template’s configuration file are applied to running instances after the polling interval. Storing the file content in the CloudFormation template keeps it with the infrastructure configuration in source control.

cfn-hup - AWS CloudFormation

questions.questionText: A company uses an HPC platform to run data-analysis jobs. The company uses AWS CodeBuild to build container images and stores the images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The images are then deployed on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). To remain compliant, the company must ensure that images are signed before deployment to Amazon EKS. The signing keys must be rotated periodically and managed automatically. The company must track who generates the signatures. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Use CodeBuild to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use AWS Signer to sign the image. Use AWS CloudTrail to track who generates the signatures.
B. Use AWS Lambda to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use a Lambda function to sign the image. Use Amazon CloudWatch to track who generates the signatures.
C. Use AWS Lambda to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use AWS Signer to sign the image. Use Amazon CloudWatch to track who generates the signatures.
D. Use CodeBuild to build the image. Sign the image by using AWS Signer before pushing the image to Amazon ECR. Use AWS CloudTrail to track who generates the signatures.
questions.explanation: AWS Signer provides managed signing and manages the signing-key lifecycle, removing the need to operate custom signing keys. Its container-image workflow signs images stored in Amazon ECR, and AWS CloudTrail records AWS Signer API activity to identify the users or accounts that generated signatures. CodeBuild can retrieve the image after it has been pushed to ECR and invoke AWS Signer, satisfying the signing and audit requirements with minimal operational overhead.

Prerequisites for signing container images

questions.questionText: A company runs an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL global database with two secondary AWS Regions. A DevOps engineer configured the database parameter group to ensure an RPO of 60 seconds. Because of the RPO configuration, write operations on the primary cluster are occasionally blocked. The DevOps engineer must reduce how often write operations are blocked. Which solution will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Add an additional secondary cluster to the global database.
B. Enable write forwarding for the global database.
C. Remove one of the secondary clusters from the global database.
D. Configure synchronous replication for the global database.
questions.explanation: For an Aurora PostgreSQL global database with rds.global_db_rpo configured, Aurora commits a transaction when at least one secondary cluster has RPO lag below the target and blocks commits only if every secondary cluster exceeds it. Adding a secondary cluster supplies another replication target that can remain within the 60-second window, reducing blocked writes while preserving the RPO requirement.

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to administer multiple accounts. Information-security policies require all unencrypted Amazon EBS volumes to be identified as noncompliant. A DevOps engineer must deploy the solution automatically and ensure that this compliance check remains in place. Which solution will achieve this?
options: A. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that defines an AWS Inspector rule to check whether EBS encryption is enabled. Save the template to an Amazon S3 bucket that has been shared with all accounts within the company. Update the account creation script pointing to the CloudFormation template in Amazon S3.

B. Create an AWS Config organizational rule to check whether EBS encryption is enabled and deploy the rule using the AWS CLI. Create and apply an SCP to prohibit stopping and deleting AWS Config across the organization.

C. Create an SCP in Organizations. Set the policy to prevent the launch of Amazon EC2 instances without encryption on the EBS volumes using a conditional expression. Apply the SCP to all AWS accounts. Use Amazon Athena to analyze the AWS CloudTrail output, looking for events that deny an ec2:RunInstances action.

D. Deploy an IAM role to all accounts from a single trusted account. Build a pipeline with AWS CodePipeline with a stage in AWS Lambda to assume the IAM role, and list all EBS volumes in the account. Publish a report to Amazon S3.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES evaluates Amazon EBS volumes and marks applicable unencrypted volumes as NON_COMPLIANT. An AWS Config organization rule deploys that managed rule throughout the organization, and an SCP can deny actions that would stop or delete AWS Config resources, helping ensure the check continues to operate in member accounts.

questions.questionText: A company operates a custom-built application that processes records. All components run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Processing each record consists of multiple sequential, compute-intensive steps. Every step always finishes in 5 minutes or less. A constraint of the current system is that, if any step fails, the application must process the record again from the start. The company wants to update the architecture so the application reprocesses only failed steps. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a web application to write records to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an EC2 instance to poll Amazon SNS and start processing. Save intermediate results to Amazon S3 to pass on to the next step.

B. Perform the processing steps by using logic in the application. Convert the application code to run in a container. Use AWS Fargate to manage the container instances. Configure the container to invoke itself to pass the state from one step to the next.
C. Create a web application to pass records to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Decouple the processing by using the Kinesis data stream and AWS Lambda functions.
D. Create a web application to pass records to AWS Step Functions. Decouple the processing into Step Functions tasks and AWS Lambda functions.
questions.explanation: AWS Step Functions provides a stateful workflow for the sequential processing stages, retaining progress between tasks and supporting task-level retry and catch behavior. Each compute stage can run as an AWS Lambda function because its maximum duration is five minutes, which is below Lambda’s 15-minute invocation limit. This eliminates the need to build and operate custom state-passing and failure-recovery logic while allowing only the failed task to be retried.
learnMore: Handling errors in Step Functions workflows
Configure Lambda function timeout

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to administer its AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer must ensure that every user who accesses the AWS Management Console authenticates through the company’s corporate identity provider (IdP). Which combination of steps satisfies these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Use Amazon GuardDuty with a delegated administrator account Use GuardDuty to enforce denial of IAM user logins.
B. Use AWS IAM Identity Center to configure identity federation with SAML 2.0.
C. Create a permissions boundary in AWS IAM Identity Center to deny password logins for IAM users.
D. Create IAM groups in the Organizations management account to apply consistent permissions for all IAM users.
E. Create an SCP in Organizations to deny password creation for IAM users.
questions.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center supports SAML 2.0 federation with an external corporate IdP, allowing workforce users to sign in with corporate credentials. IAM-user console access requires an IAM user password (a login profile); an AWS Organizations service control policy can act as an organization-wide permissions guardrail to deny creation of those passwords. Together, these controls provide federated console authentication while preventing new IAM-user password logins. External identity providers — AWS IAM Identity Center Policy evaluation logic — AWS IAM create-login-profile — AWS CLI

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is configuring an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) blue/green deployment for an application by using AWS CodeDeploy and AWS CloudFormation. During the deployment window, the application must remain highly available, and CodeDeploy must shift 10% of traffic to a new application version every minute until all traffic has shifted. Which configuration should the DevOps engineer add to the CloudFormation template to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Add an AppSpec file with the CodeDeployDefault.ECSLinearl OPercentEveryl Minutes deployment configuration.
B. Add the AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen transform and the AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen hook parameter with the CodeDeployDefault.ECSLinear10PercentEvery1Minutes deployment configuration.
C. Add an AppSpec file with the ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes deployment configuration.
D. Add the AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen transform and the AWS::CodeDepioy::BlueGreen hook parameter with the ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes deployment configuration.
questions.explanation: CloudFormation-managed ECS blue/green deployments use the AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen transform together with an AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen hook. CodeDeployDefault.ECSLinear10PercentEvery1Minutes is the predefined ECS deployment configuration that shifts 10% of traffic every minute until all traffic is shifted.

questions.questionText: A company plans to use AWS development tools to replace its existing bash deployment scripts. It currently deploys a LAMP application to a set of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). During deployments, the company unit tests the committed application, stops and starts services, unregisters and re-registers instances with the load balancer, and updates file permissions. The company wants to retain the same deployment functionality while moving to AWS services. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CodeBuild to test the application. Use bash scripts invoked by AWS CodeDeploy's appspec.yml file to restart services, and deregister and register instances with the ALB. Use the appspec.yml file to update file permissions without a custom script.

B. Use AWS CodePipeline to move the application from the AWS CodeCommit repository to AWS CodeDeploy. Use CodeDeploy's deployment group to test the application, unregister and re-register instances with the ALand restart services. Use the appspec.yml file to update file permissions without a custom script.

C. Use AWS CodePipeline to move the application source code from the AWS CodeCommit repository to AWS CodeDeploy. Use CodeDeploy to test the application. Use CodeDeploy's appspec.yml file to restart services and update permissions without a custom script. Use AWS CodeBuild to unregister and re-register instances with the ALB.

D. Use AWS CodePipeline to trigger AWS CodeBuild to test the application. Use bash scripts invoked by AWS CodeDeploy's appspec.yml file to restart services. Unregister and re-register the instances in the AWS CodeDeploy deployment group with the ALB. Update the appspec.yml file to update file permissions without a custom script.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild can run the application's unit tests. For EC2/on-premises deployments, a CodeDeploy AppSpec file can invoke scripts at lifecycle hooks, including scripts that stop and restart services, and its permissions section applies file permissions without a custom script. When an ALB target group is configured in an in-place CodeDeploy deployment group, CodeDeploy deregisters each instance during its deployment and registers it again after the deployment succeeds.

questions.questionText: A security team configures a workflow that starts an AWS Step Functions workflow when Amazon EventBridge matches particular events. Several AWS services can generate these events. AWS CloudTrail records user activity. The security team finds that some significant events do not start the workflow as anticipated. The CloudTrail logs show no direct errors associated with the missing events. Which combination of steps will identify the root cause of the missing event invocations? Choose three
options: A. Enable EventBridge schema discovery on the event bus to determine whether the event patterns match the expected schema.
B. Configure Amazon CloudWatch to monitor EventBridge metrics and Step Functions metrics. Set up alerts for anomalies in event patterns and workflow invocations.
C. Configure an AWS Lambda logging function to monitor and log events from EventBridge to provide more details about the processed events.
D. Review the Step Functions execution history for patterns of failures or timeouts that could correlate to the missing event invocations.
E. Review metrics for the EventBridge failed invocations to ensure that the IAM execution role that is attached to the rule has sufficient permissions.
questions.explanation: EventBridge only routes events whose structure and values satisfy the rule’s event pattern, so discovering schemas helps validate the pattern against actual events. Amazon CloudWatch provides EventBridge rule metrics for invocation attempts and permanent failures, while Step Functions metrics help reveal downstream workflow behavior. A nonzero EventBridge FailedInvocations metric identifies permanent target-delivery failures; for a Step Functions target, the EventBridge execution role must permit states:StartExecution on the state machine.
learnMore: Monitoring Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer administers a company's Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The cluster runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution that logs and reviews every stopped task for errors. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to capture task state changes. Send the event to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to investigate stopped tasks.
B. Configure tasks to write log data in the embedded metric format. Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Monitor the ContainerInstanceCount metric for changes.

C. Configure the EC2 instances to store logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule that uses the EC2 instance log data. Use the Contributor Insights rule to investigate stopped tasks.
D. Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hook for the EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING scale-in event. Write the SystemEventLog file to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the log file for errors.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECS publishes task state change events to Amazon EventBridge. Events for stopped tasks include details such as the stop code and stopped reason. An EventBridge rule can route these events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, where CloudWatch Logs Insights can retain, filter, and investigate stopped-task errors.

The company also requires a dashboard that displays any log activity generated by the root user. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Enable AWS Config with a multi-account aggregator. Configure log forwarding to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
B. Create an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that uses an Amazon CloudWatch Logs query.

C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric filter to match root user login events. Configure a CloudWatch alarm and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send alerts to the company's monitoring system.

D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to match root user login events. Configure the filter to forward events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure the SNS topic to send alerts to the company's monitoring system.
E. Create an AWS CloudTrail organization trail. Configure the organization trail to send events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
questions.explanation: An AWS CloudTrail organization trail records activity across the organization and can deliver those events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. A CloudWatch Logs metric filter can identify root-user sign-in events and produce a metric that a CloudWatch alarm uses to invoke an Amazon SNS notification. A CloudWatch dashboard can include a CloudWatch Logs Insights query to display root-user log activity.

questions.questionText: A DevOps team has created a custom AWS Config Lambda rule. The rule monitors Amazon Elastic Container Repository (Amazon ECR) policy statements for ecr:* actions. When it detects a noncompliant repository, Amazon EventBridge uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to route the notification to a security team. When AWS Config evaluates the custom rule, the AWS Lambda function does not run. Which solution will fix the issue?
options: A. Modify the Lambda function's resource policy to grant AWS Config permission to invoke the function.
B. Modify the SNS topic policy to include configuration changes for EventBridge to publish to the SNS topic.
C. Modify the Lambda function's execution role to include configuration changes for custom AWS Config rules.
D. Modify all the ECR repository policies to grant AWS Config access to the necessary ECR API actions.
questions.explanation: AWS Config invokes the Lambda function associated with a custom Lambda rule. An AWS service needs lambda:InvokeFunction permission through the function’s resource-based policy to invoke that function; therefore, the function policy must grant AWS Config permission. The execution role applies to actions performed by the function after invocation, not to AWS Config’s ability to invoke it. Creating AWS Config Custom Lambda Rules, Granting Lambda function access to AWS services

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer provisioned an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster using managed node groups. The DevOps engineer associated an OpenID Connect (OIDC) issuer with the cluster. The DevOps engineer is configuring Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSD (gp3) volumes for the cluster. The DevOps engineer tries to initiate a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) request but cannot provision a volume. To troubleshoot the issue, the DevOps engineer runs the kubectl describe pyc command. The DevOps engineer receives a failed to provision volume with StorageClass error and a could not create volume in EC2:UnauthorizedOperation error. Which solution will resolve these errors?
options: A. Create a Kubernetes cluster role that allows the persistent volumes to perform get, list, watch, create, and delete operations. Configure the cluster role to allow get, list, and watch operations for storage in the cluster.

B. Create an Amazon EBS Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver IAM role that has the required permissions and trust relationships. Attach the IAM role to the Amazon EBS CSI driver add-on in the cluster.
C. Add the ebs.csi.aws.com/volumeType:gp3 annotation to the PersistentVolumeClaim object in the cluster.
D. Create a Kubernetes storage class object. Set the provisioner value to ebs.csi.aws.com. Set the volumeBindingMode value to WaitForFirstConsumer in the luster.
questions.explanation: The Amazon EBS CSI driver requires an IAM role with permissions to call the required Amazon EC2 APIs and an appropriate trust relationship. Associating that role with the EBS CSI driver add-on gives the controller the credentials needed to create gp3 EBS volumes. Without this configuration, PVC provisioning can fail with failed to provision volume with StorageClass and could not create volume in EC2: UnauthorizedOperation.
learnMore: Use Kubernetes volume storage with Amazon EBS

questions.questionText: A company application exposes an API that retrieves workload metrics. The company must audit, analyze, and visualize the application’s metrics to identify issues at scale. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Configure an Amazon EventBridge schedule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that calls the API to retrieve workload metrics. Store the workload metric data in an Amazon S3 bucket.

B. Configure an Amazon EventBridge schedule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that calls the API to retrieve workload metrics. Store the workload metric data in an Amazon DynamoDB table that has a DynamoDB stream enabled.
C. Create an AWS Glue crawler to catalog the workload metric data in the Amazon S3 bucket. Create views in Amazon Athena for the cataloged data.
D. Connect an AWS Glue crawler to the Amazon DynamoDB stream to catalog the workload metric data. Create views in Amazon Athena for the cataloged data.
E. Create Amazon QuickSight datasets from the Amazon Athena views. Create a QuickSight analysis to visualize the workload metric data as a dashboard.

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that installs antivirus software on every Amazon EC2 instance in an AWS account. The EC2 instances are running the latest version of Amazon Linux. The solution must identify all instances and use an AWS Systems Manager document to install the software when it is not already installed. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an association in Systems Manager State Manager. Target all the managed nodes. Include the software in the association. Configure the association to use the Systems Manager document.

B. Set up AWS Config to record all the resources in the account. Create an AWS Config custom rule to determine if the software is installed on all the EC2 instances. Configure an automatic remediation action that uses the Systems Manager document for noncompliant EC2 instances.
C. Activate Amazon EC2 scanning on Amazon Inspector to determine if the software is installed on all the EC2 instances. Associate the findings with the Systems Manager document.

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses AWS CloudTrail to detect the Runinstances API call. Configure inventory collection in Systems Manager Inventory to determine if the software is installed on the EC2 instances. Associate the Systems Manager inventory with the Systems Manager document.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager State Manager associations maintain a specified state on managed nodes. An association can target all managed nodes in the account and use an SSM document that checks for antivirus software and installs it when absent. State Manager also applies the association to newly detected target nodes, providing ongoing enforcement. AWS Systems Manager State Manager
