Accessing member accounts in an organization with AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: A company uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to define its application. It uses a pipeline consisting of AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to deploy the CDK application. The company wants to add unit tests to the pipeline to test various infrastructure components. It must ensure that deployment proceeds only when no unit test fails. Which combination of steps will enforce the testing requirement in the pipeline? Choose two
options: A. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Set the OnFailure phase property to ABORT.
B. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Add the --rollback true flag to the cdk deploy command.
C. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Add the --require-approval any-change flag to the cdk deploy command.
D. Create a test that uses the AWS CDK assertions module. Use the template.hasResourceProperties assertion to test that resources have the expected properties.
E. Create a test that uses the cdk diff command. Configure the test to fail if any resources have changed.
questions.explanation: AWS CDK’s assertions module supports unit testing of synthesized CloudFormation templates, and template.hasResourceProperties verifies that a resource of a specified type has the expected properties. CodeBuild’s on-failure: ABORT setting aborts the build phase when a test command fails, preventing the subsequent cdk deploy command from running.
learnMore: Build specification reference for CodeBuild
Test AWS CDK applications

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company’s development team uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy its application resources. Question 194 / Configuration Management and IaC A company’s development team uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy its application resources. The team must use CloudFormation for every environment change and cannot use the AWS Management Console or AWS CLI to make manual changes directly. The team accesses the environment by using a developer IAM role configured with the AdministratorAccess managed IAM policy. The company created a new CloudFormationDeployment IAM role with the following policy attached: The company must ensure that only CloudFormation can use the new role. The development team must not be able to make manual changes to deployed resources. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Remove the AdministratorAccess policy. Assign the ReadOnlyAccess managed IAM policy to the developer role. Instruct the developers to use the CloudFormationDeployment role as a CloudFormation service role when the developers deploy new stacks.
B. Update the trust policy of the CloudFormationDeployment role to allow the developer IAM role to assume the CloudFormationDeployment role.

C. Configure the developer IAM role to be able to get and pass the CloudFormationDeployment role if iam:PassedToService equals . Configure the CloudFormationDeployment role to allow all cloudformation actions for all resources.
D. Update the trust policy of the CloudFormationDeployment role to allow the cloudformation.amazonaws.com AWS principal to perform the iam:AssumeRole action.

E. Remove the AdministratorAccess policy. Assign the ReadOnlyAccess managed IAM policy to the developer role. Instruct the developers to assume the CloudFormationDeployment role when the developers deploy new stacks.
questions.explanation: A CloudFormation service role lets CloudFormation perform stack resource operations using the role’s permissions rather than the developer’s permissions. Developers must not retain AdministratorAccess, because it permits direct changes; they should use the deployment role only as the CloudFormation service role. The role trust policy must allow cloudformation.amazonaws.com to perform sts:AssumeRole, preventing developers from assuming it directly. The developer-facing permission to pass the role must be restricted to that role and conditioned on iam:PassedToService being cloudformation.amazonaws.com, so the role can be supplied only to CloudFormation.

Service roles for CloudFormation

questions.questionText: A company has multiple accounts within an AWS Organizations organization. The company's SecOps team must receive an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if any account in the organization disables the Block Public Access feature on an Amazon S3 bucket. A DevOps engineer must implement this change without affecting the operation of any AWS accounts. The implementation must ensure that individual member accounts in the organization cannot disable the notification. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Designate an account to be the delegated Amazon GuardDuty administrator account. Turn on GuardDuty for all accounts across the organization. In the GuardDuty administrator account, create an SNS topic. Subscribe the SecOps team's email address to the SNS topic. In the same account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses an event pattern for GuardDuty findings and a target of the SNS topic.

B. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that creates an SNS topic and subscribes the SecOps team’s email address to the SNS topic. In the template, include an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses an event pattern of CloudTrail activity for s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock and a target of the SNS topic. Deploy the stack to every account in the organization by using CloudFormation StackSets.

C. Turn on AWS Config across the organization. In the delegated administrator account, create an SNS topic. Subscribe the SecOps team's email address to the SNS topic. Deploy a conformance pack that uses the s3-bucket-level-public-access-prohibited AWS Config managed rule in each account and uses an AWS Systems Manager document to publish an event to the SNS topic to notify the SecOps team.

D. Turn on Amazon Inspector across the organization. In the Amazon Inspector delegated administrator account, create an SNS topic. Subscribe the SecOps team’s email address to the SNS topic. In the same account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses an event pattern for public network exposure of the S3 bucket and publishes an event to the SNS topic to notify the SecOps team.
questions.explanation: AWS Config can evaluate bucket-level Block Public Access settings with the s3-bucket-level-public-access-prohibited managed rule and can use an AWS Systems Manager Automation document as a remediation action to publish to Amazon SNS when a resource is noncompliant. An organization conformance pack centrally deploys the rule and remediation across member accounts; AWS Config organization conformance-pack APIs are available only to the management account or a delegated administrator, preventing member accounts from disabling that centrally managed control.

questions.questionText: A company runs an application in its AWS account. The application uses an Amazon S3 bucket to store objects that include sensitive information. The company must capture object-level S3 API calls, including calls that are rejected because they use invalid credentials. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS CloudTrail trail in the account. Enable S3 data events logging. Configure the trail to log to Amazon CloudWatch.
B. Create a new S3 bucket. Configure access logging on the application's S3 bucket. Deliver the access logs to the new S3 bucket.

C. Configure Amazon GuardDuty with S3 protection enabled for the account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches findings that are associated with the S3 bucket. Configure the rule to use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the target.
D. Create an AWS CloudTrail trail and a new S3 bucket in the account. Configure the trail to log to the S3 new bucket.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 server access logging provides detailed records of requests made to a bucket and delivers them to a destination S3 bucket. AWS CloudTrail data events record object-level S3 operations, but CloudTrail does not deliver logs for requests that fail authentication because the provided credentials are invalid. Therefore, S3 server access logging is required for this condition.
learnMore: Logging options for Amazon S3
Logging requests with server access logging

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer plans to use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to manage infrastructure as code (IaC) for a microservices-based application. The engineer must build reusable components for common infrastructure patterns and apply identical cost-allocation tags across the different microservices. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a custom CDK construct library that includes common infrastructure patterns. Create a CDK app. Use the TagManager class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the custom CDK construct library to write a higher-level construct that contains all the microservices. Deploy the microservices as a single CDK stack with environment-specific configurations

B. Create a custom CDK construct library that includes common infrastructure patterns. Create a CDK app. Use the Tags class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the custom CDK construct library to write higher-level constructs for each microservice. Deploy the microservices as separate CDK stacks with environment-specific configurations.

C. Create AWS Service Catalog products that contain common infrastructure components. Create a CDK app. Use the TagManager class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the Service Catalog products to write a higher-level construct that contains all the microservices. Deploy the microservices as a single CDK stack with environment-specific configurations.

D. Create AWS Service Catalog products that contain common infrastructure components. Create a CDK app. Use the Tags class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the Service Catalog products to write higher-level constructs for each microservice. Deploy the microservices as separate CDK stacks with environment-specific configurations.
questions.explanation: AWS CDK constructs are reusable, composable infrastructure components and can be packaged in a custom construct library. Tags.of(app).add() applies a tag throughout the app’s construct scope to taggable child resources, making it suitable for consistent cost-allocation tags. Higher-level constructs can model each microservice, while separate CDK stacks provide independent deployment units for those services.
learnMore: Tags and the AWS CDK

questions.questionText: A company hosts a web application on Amazon EC2 instances and is deploying the application across multiple AWS Regions. The application includes dynamic content, such as WebSocket-based, real-time product updates. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to manage all DNS records. Which solution provides multi-Region access to the application with the least latency?
options: A. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Create a Route 53 A record with a latency-based routing policy. Add IP addresses of the ALBs as the value of the record.

B. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin group that contains the ALBs as origins. Create a Route 53 alias record that points to the CloudFront distribution's DNS address.

C. Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Create a Route 53 A record with a multivalue answer routing policy. Add IP addresses of the NLBs as the value of the record.

D. Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator with an endpoint group for each NLB. Create a Route 53 alias record that points to the accelerator's DNS address.
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides anycast static IP entry points at AWS edge locations and routes TCP traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal healthy regional endpoint. A standard accelerator supports Network Load Balancers as endpoints, making it suitable for low-latency, dynamic WebSocket traffic across multiple Regions. CloudFront origin groups provide primary/secondary origin failover rather than latency-based distribution among regional origins.
learnMore: How AWS Global Accelerator works
Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator

questions.questionText: A software team uses AWS CodePipeline to automate the release pipeline for its Java application. The pipeline has a source stage, followed by a build stage, followed by a deploy stage. Each stage includes one action with a runOrder value of 1. The team wants to incorporate unit testing into the current release pipeline. The solution must deploy only code changes that pass every unit test. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Modify the build stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 1. Use AWS CodeDeploy as the action provider to run unit tests.
B. Modify the build stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 2. Use AWS CodeBuild as the action provider to run unit tests.
C. Modify the deploy stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 1. Use AWS CodeDeploy as the action provider to run unit tests.
D. Modify the deploy stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 2. Use AWS CodeBuild as the action provider to run unit tests.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild supports CodePipeline Test actions and runs the test commands defined for the build project. Adding that test action to the build stage with runOrder 2 causes it to run after the existing build action (runOrder 1); the pipeline cannot advance to the deploy stage unless the test action succeeds. AWS CodeDeploy is a Deploy action provider, not a Test action provider.
learnMore: Action declaration - AWS CodePipeline

questions.questionText: A company has recently deployed its web application on AWS. The company is preparing for a large-scale sales event and must ensure the web application can scale to satisfy demand. The application's frontend infrastructure includes an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as its origin. The backend infrastructure includes an Amazon API Gateway API, several AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon Aurora DB cluster. The company's DevOps engineer performs a load test and determines that the Lambda functions can fulfill the peak number of requests. However, the DevOps engineer observes request latency during the initial burst of requests. Most requests to the Lambda functions generate database queries. Establishing database connections accounts for a large portion of invocation time. Which combination of steps will provide the required scalability? Choose three
options: A. Configure a higher reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions.
B. Configure a higher provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions.
C. Convert the DB cluster to an Aurora global database. Add additional Aurora Replicas in AWS Regions based on the locations of the company's customers.
D. Refactor the Lambda functions. Move the code blocks that initialize database connections into the function handlers.
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda provisioned concurrency keeps a configured number of execution environments pre-initialized and ready to respond, reducing cold-start latency during an initial request burst. Amazon RDS Proxy pools and manages shared database connections, allowing Lambda to reach high concurrency without repeatedly creating connections or exhausting Aurora connections. An Aurora Global Database with Aurora Replicas in customer Regions supplies local-latency read capacity and lets each secondary cluster scale its read workload independently.
learnMore: Configuring reserved concurrency for a function — AWS Lambda

questions.questionText: A company policy requires every Amazon EC2 instance to be launched from an AMI produced by the company’s security team. Each month, the security team emails all development teams a message containing the newest approved AMIs. The development teams deploy their applications with AWS CloudFormation. When developers launch a new service, they must search their email for the latest AMIs sent by the security department. A DevOps engineer wants to automate the process by which the security team provides AMI IDs to the development teams. What is the MOST scalable solution that satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Direct the security team to use CloudFormation to create new versions of the AMIs and to list the AMI ARNs in an encrypted Amazon S3 object as part of the stack’s Outputs section. Instruct the developers to use a cross-stack reference to load the encrypted S3 object and obtain the most recent AMI ARNs.

B. Direct the security team to use a CloudFormation stack to create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that builds new AMIs and places the latest AMI ARNs in an encrypted Amazon S3 object as part of the pipeline output. Instruct the developers to use a cross-stack reference within their own CloudFormation template to obtain the S3 object location and the most recent AMI ARNs.

C. Direct the security team to use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create new AMIs and to place the AMI ARNs as parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Instruct the developers to specify a parameter of type SSM in their CloudFormation stack to obtain the most recent AMI ARNs from Parameter Store.

D. Direct the security team to use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create new AMIs and to create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic so that every development team can receive notifications. When the development teams receive a notification, instruct them to write an AWS Lambda function that will update their CloudFormation stack with the most recent AMI ARNs.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Image Builder can produce the approved AMIs, while AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store provides a centralized, versioned location for the current approved AMI ID. CloudFormation supports Systems Manager parameter types, including AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<AWS::EC2::Image::Id>, and retrieves the latest parameter value for stack use. This lets all development teams consistently consume the approved AMI without manual email lookup or team-specific update automation.

questions.questionText: A company runs a stateless web application deployed on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in a target group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Amazon Route 53 manages the application's domain. The company updates the application UI and creates a beta version of the application. The company needs to test the beta version with 10% of its traffic. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST number of configuration changes?
options: A. Deploy the beta version to new EC2 instances in a new target group. Associate the new target group with a new ALB. Update the existing Route 53 record to use a weighted routing policy. Add a new Route 53 record that points to the new ALB with the same routing policy. Assign a weight of 90 to the existing record. Assign a weight of 10 to the new record.

B. Deploy the beta version to new EC2 instances in a new target group. Associate the new target group with the same ALB listener rule. Assign a weight of 90 to the existing target group. Assign a weight of 10 to the new target group.
C. Refactor the application to implement a feature flag for the beta version by using AWS AppConfig. Use the feature flag to enable the beta version for 10% of the EC2 instances.

D. Containerize and deploy the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the beta version by using the CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes deployment configuration.
questions.explanation: An Application Load Balancer listener rule can use a forward action with multiple target groups and relative weights. Setting the existing target group to 90 and the beta target group to 10 directs approximately 90% and 10% of matching requests, respectively, while retaining the existing ALB and Route 53 configuration.
learnMore: Action types for listener rules - Elastic Load Balancing

questions.questionText: A DevOps team supports an application running in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The team currently uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the application with a blue/green all-at-once strategy. Recently, the team had to roll back a deployment because a new application version dramatically increased request response times. The DevOps team needs to use a deployment strategy that lets the team monitor a new application version before shifting all traffic to it. If a new application version increases response times, the deployment must be rolled back as quickly as possible. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Modify the CodeDeploy deployment to use the CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes configuration.
B. Modify the CodeDeploy deployment to use the CodeDeployDefault.ECSLinear10PercentEvery3Minutes configuration.

C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor the UnHealthyHostCount metric for the ALB. Set the alarm to activate if the metric is higher than the desired value. Associate the alarm with the CodeDeploy deployment group. Modify the deployment group to roll back when a deployment fails.

D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor the TargetResponseTime metric for the ALB. Set the alarm to activate if the metric is higher than the desired value. Associate the alarm with the CodeDeploy deployment group. Modify the deployment group to roll back when alarm thresholds are met.

E. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor the TargetConnectionErrorCount metric for the ALB. Set the alarm to activate if the metric is higher than the desired value. Associate the alarm with the CodeDeploy deployment group. Modify the deployment group to roll back when alarm thresholds are met.
questions.explanation: The CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes configuration shifts 10% of traffic first and delays the remaining 90% for five minutes, allowing the replacement version to be observed before it receives all traffic. The ALB TargetResponseTime metric directly measures the reported performance degradation. A CloudWatch alarm on that metric, associated with the CodeDeploy deployment group and configured to roll back when alarm thresholds are met, automatically redeploys the last known good revision when the response-time threshold is breached.
learnMore: Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy
Configure advanced options for a deployment group

questions.questionText: A company’s DevOps engineer uses AWS Systems Manager to carry out maintenance work during maintenance windows. A few Amazon EC2 instances must be restarted after AWS Health notifications. The DevOps engineer must implement an automated solution to remediate these notifications and creates an Amazon EventBridge rule. How should the DevOps engineer configure the EventBridge rule to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Configure an event source of AWS Health, a service of EC2. and an event type that indicates instance maintenance. Target a Systems Manager document to restart the EC2 instance.
B. Configure an event source of Systems Manager and an event type that indicates a maintenance window. Target a Systems Manager document to restart the EC2 instance.

C. Configure an event source of AWS Health, a service of EC2, and an event type that indicates instance maintenance. Target a newly created AWS Lambda function that registers an automation task to restart the EC2 instance during a maintenance window.

D. Configure an event source of EC2 and an event type that indicates instance maintenance. Target a newly created AWS Lambda function that registers an automation task to restart the EC2 instance during a maintenance window.
questions.explanation: AWS Health EC2 scheduled-change events are the appropriate EventBridge source for instance-maintenance notifications. Because the restart must occur during a Systems Manager maintenance window, a Lambda target can use the event’s affected instance information to register an Automation task with that maintenance window; Systems Manager runs registered Automation tasks during the scheduled maintenance period. A direct Systems Manager document target would run when EventBridge receives the event rather than queueing the action for the maintenance window.
learnMore: Running operations on EC2 instances automatically in response to events in AWS Health
Schedule automations with maintenance windows

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company uses an AWS CodeBuild project to build and package an application. Question 207 / Security and Compliance A company uses an AWS CodeBuild project to build and package an application. Before deployment across multiple AWS accounts, the packages are copied to a shared Amazon S3 bucket. The buildspec.yml file includes the following: A DevOps engineer has discovered that anyone with an AWS account can download the artifacts. What should the DevOps engineer do to prevent this?
options: A. Modify the post_build command to use --acl public-read and configure a bucket policy that grants read access to the relevant AWS accounts only.
B. Configure a default ACL for the S3 bucket that defines the set of authenticated users as the relevant AWS accounts only and grants read-only access.
C. Create an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the relevant AWS accounts and denies read access to the principal “*”.
D. Modify the post_build command to remove --acl authenticated-read and configure a bucket policy that allows read access to the relevant AWS accounts only.
questions.explanation: The authenticated-read S3 canned ACL grants read access to the Authenticated Users group, which includes all AWS accounts making signed requests. Remove that ACL from the upload command and use a bucket policy that explicitly allows read access only to the relevant AWS accounts. A policy Allow alone would not negate the existing broad ACL, and a Deny for principal * would override the intended accounts’ Allow permissions.
learnMore: Access control list (ACL) overview
How Amazon S3 authorizes a request

questions.questionText: A company has selected AWS to host a new application and must implement a multi-account strategy. A DevOps engineer creates a new AWS account and an organization in AWS Organizations. The DevOps engineer also creates the organization's OU structure and establishes a landing zone by using AWS Control Tower. The DevOps engineer must implement a solution that automatically deploys resources for new accounts that users create through AWS Control Tower Account Factory. When a user creates a new account, the solution must apply AWS CloudFormation templates and SCPs customized for the OU or account to automatically deploy all resources attached to that account. All OUs are enrolled in AWS Control Tower. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST automated way?
options: A. Use AWS Service Catalog with AWS Control Tower. Create portfolios and products in AWS Service Catalog. Grant granular permissions to provision these resources. Deploy SCPs by using the AWS CLI and JSON documents.

B. Deploy CloudFormation stack sets by using the required templates. Enable automatic deployment. Deploy stack instances to the required accounts. Deploy a CloudFormation stack set to the organization’s management account to deploy SCPs.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect the CreateManagedAccount event. Configure AWS Service Catalog as the target to deploy resources to any new accounts. Deploy SCPs by using the AWS CLI and JSON documents.

D. Deploy the Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) solution. Use an AWS CodeCommit repository as the source. In the repository, create a custom package that includes the CloudFormation templates and the SCP JSON documents.
questions.explanation: Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) integrates CloudFormation templates and service control policies (SCPs) with AWS Control Tower lifecycle events. It automatically deploys custom resources and policies to targeted accounts or OUs when an Account Factory account is created. A CfCT configuration package can use AWS CodeCommit as its source and includes CloudFormation template files and SCP JSON policy files.
learnMore: Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) overview
Define a custom configuration for CfCT

questions.questionText: A company has numerous applications. Different teams developed the applications using multiple languages and frameworks. The applications run on premises and on various servers with different operating systems. Each team has its own release protocol and process. The company wants to reduce the complexity of releasing and maintaining these applications. The company is migrating its technology stacks, including these applications, to AWS. It wants centralized source-code control, a consistent and automated delivery pipeline, and as few maintenance tasks as possible for the underlying infrastructure. What should a DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for all applications. Put each application's code in a different branch. Merge the branches, and use AWS CodeBuild to build the applications. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the applications to one centralized application server.

B. Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for each of the applications. Use AWS CodeBuild to build the applications one at a time. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the applications to one centralized application server.

C. Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for each of the applications. Use AWS CodeBuild to build the applications one at a time and to create one AMI for each server. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to automatically provision and decommission Amazon EC2 fleets by using these AMIs.

D. Create one AWS CodeCommit repository for each of the applications. Use AWS CodeBuild to build one Docker image for each application in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on infrastructure that AWS Fargate manages.
questions.explanation: Docker images package each application with its dependencies, creating a consistent deployment unit despite different languages, frameworks, and operating systems. CodeBuild can build and push those images to Amazon ECR, while CodeDeploy supports deployments to Amazon ECS. Running ECS tasks on AWS Fargate removes server and EC2 fleet management, satisfying the requirement to minimize underlying-infrastructure maintenance. Separate CodeCommit repositories also support centralized source control without combining independent applications into branches of one repository.
learnMore: Publish Docker image to an Amazon ECR image repository sample for CodeBuild
Deployments on an Amazon ECS Compute Platform

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer uses AWS CodeDeploy across a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group. The related CodeDeploy deployment group, integrated with EC2 Auto Scaling, is configured for in-place deployments with CodeDeployDefault.OneAtATime. During an ongoing new deployment, the engineer finds that, although the overall deployment completed successfully, two of five instances have the prior application revision deployed. The other three instances have the latest application revision. What is the likely cause of this issue?
options: A. The two affected instances failed to fetch the new deployment.
B. A failed AfterInstall lifecycle event hook caused the CodeDeploy agent to roll back to the previous version on the affected instances.
C. The CodeDeploy agent was not installed in two affected instances.
D. EC2 Auto Scaling launched two new instances while the new deployment had not yet finished, causing the previous version to be deployed on the affected instances.
questions.explanation: When an EC2 Auto Scaling scale-out event occurs while a CodeDeploy deployment is in progress, CodeDeploy deploys the previously deployed application revision—not the new revision—to the new instances. A successful deployment can therefore leave the original and newly scaled-out instances on different revisions until CodeDeploy performs its follow-on update of outdated instances.
learnMore: Integrating CodeDeploy with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling

questions.questionText: A company operates an application in an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances run Docker containers that send requests to a MySQL database running on separate EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer must update the application to use a serverless architecture. Which solution meets this requirement with the fewest changes?
options: A. Replace the containers that run on EC2 instances and the ALB with AWS Lambda functions. Replace the MySQL database with an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database that is compatible with MySQL.
B. Replace the containers that run on EC2 instances with AWS Fargate. Replace the MySQL database with an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database that is compatible with MySQL.
C. Replace the containers that run on EC2 instances and the ALB with AWS Lambda functions. Replace the MySQL database with Amazon DynamoDB tables.
D. Replace the containers that run on EC2 instances with AWS Fargate. Replace the MySQL database with Amazon DynamoDB tables.
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate is serverless compute for containers, allowing the existing Docker containers to run without managing EC2 instances and to remain behind the ALB. Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 supports an Aurora MySQL-compatible engine, so the existing relational MySQL data model and SQL-based access require substantially fewer changes than a migration to DynamoDB. AWS Fargate Decision Guide, Creating an Aurora Serverless v2 DB cluster
learnMore: Creating an Aurora Serverless v2 DB cluster

questions.questionText: A DevOps team is integrating code revisions for an application that uses an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster as its production database. The team uses continuous integration to periodically confirm that the application functions correctly. The team must test the changes before deploying them to the production database. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use a buildspec file in AWS CodeBuild to restore the DB cluster from a snapshot of the production database, run integration tests, and drop the restored database after verification.
B. Deploy the application to production. Configure an audit log of data control language (DCL) operations to capture database activities to perform if verification fails.

C. Create a snapshot of the DB cluster before deploying the application. Use the Update requires:Replacement property on the DB instance in AWS CloudFormation to deploy the application and apply the changes.
D. Ensure that the DB cluster is a Multi-AZ deployment. Deploy the application with the updates. Fail over to the standby instance if verification fails.
questions.explanation: Restoring a production database snapshot into a separate DB cluster provides an isolated copy of production data for integration testing before production deployment. Amazon RDS supports restoring a Multi-AZ DB cluster snapshot to a new DB cluster, allowing the temporary test database to be removed after verification. Restoring from a snapshot to a Multi-AZ DB cluster
learnMore: Restoring from a snapshot to a Multi-AZ DB cluster

questions.questionText: A company has an AWS CodePipeline pipeline in the eu-west-1 Region. The pipeline keeps build artifacts in an Amazon S3 bucket. It builds and deploys an AWS Lambda function through an AWS CloudFormation deploy action. A DevOps engineer must update the existing pipeline so that it also deploys the Lambda function to the us-east-1 Region. The pipeline has already been updated to produce an additional artifact for deployment to us-east-1. Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Modify the CloudFormation template to include a parameter for the Lambda function code's .zip file location. Create a new CloudFormation deploy action for us-east-1 in the pipeline. Configure the new deploy action to pass in the us-east-1 artifact location as a parameter override.

B. Create a new CloudFormation deploy action for us-east-1 in the pipeline. Configure the new deploy action to use the CloudFormation template from the additional artifact that was created for us-east-1.
C. Create an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure the S3 bucket policy to allow CodePipeline to have read and write access.
D. Create an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the S3 bucket in eu-west-1 to the S3 bucket in us-east-1.

E. Modify the pipeline to include the S3 bucket for us-east-1 as an artifact store. Create a new CloudFormation deploy action for us-east-1 in the pipeline. Configure the new deploy action to use the CloudFormation template from the us-east-1 artifact.
questions.explanation: Each Region that contains a CodePipeline action needs its own regional artifact store. A us-east-1 S3 bucket must therefore be created and added to the pipeline’s artifactStores, and a CloudFormation deploy action in us-east-1 must use the us-east-1 artifact. CodePipeline copies input artifacts across Regions for cross-Region actions, so S3 Cross-Region Replication is unnecessary.
learnMore: Add a cross-Region action in CodePipeline
ArtifactStore - CodePipeline API Reference

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company is assessing its IAM policies. Question 214 / Security and Compliance A company is assessing its IAM policies. A policy authored by the DevOps engineer has been identified as overly permissive. An AWS Lambda function uses the policy to issue a stop command to Amazon EC2 instances tagged with Environment: NonProduction during the weekend. The current policy is: Which changes should the engineer make to implement a least-privilege policy? Choose three
options: A.
B. Change "Resource": ""to "Resource": "arn:aws:ec2:::instance/"
C.
D.
E. Change "Action": "ec2:*"to "Action": "ec2:StopInstances"
questions.explanation: Least privilege grants only ec2:StopInstances, limits the resource to EC2 instance ARNs, and uses StringEquals with ec2:ResourceTag/Environment set to NonProduction so that only appropriately tagged instances can be stopped. Amazon EC2 supports instance resources and resource-tag condition keys in IAM policies. IAM date condition operators compare against specified date/time values; they do not support policy variables for a recurring weekday expression.
learnMore: Actions, resources, and condition keys for Amazon EC2

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is configuring a container-based architecture. The engineer has chosen AWS CloudFormation to automatically provision an Amazon ECS cluster and an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group that launches the EC2 container instances. After the CloudFormation stack was created successfully, the engineer observed that, although the ECS cluster and EC2 instances were created successfully and stack creation completed, the EC2 instances were associating with a different cluster. How should the DevOps engineer update the CloudFormation template to fix this issue?
options: A. Reference the EC2 instances in the AWS::ECS::Cluster resource and reference the ECS cluster in the AWS::ECS::Service resource.
B. Reference the ECS cluster in the AWS::AutoScaling::LaunchConfiguration resource of the UserData property.
C. Reference the ECS cluster in the AWS::EC2::Instance resource of the UserData property.
D. Reference the ECS cluster in the AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource resource to trigger an AWS Lambda function that registers the EC2 instances with the appropriate ECS cluster.
questions.explanation: EC2 container instances launched through an Auto Scaling group use the launch configuration's UserData at startup. The ECS agent joins the default cluster unless UserData configures ECS_CLUSTER with the intended cluster name. Referencing the ECS cluster in AWS::AutoScaling::LaunchConfiguration UserData ensures every Auto Scaling–launched container instance registers with that cluster.

Launching an Amazon ECS Linux container instance

questions.questionText: A company has created a static website hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket. The website is deployed with AWS CloudFormation. The CloudFormation template defines an S3 bucket and a custom resource that copies content from a source location into the bucket. The company has determined that it must move the website to a new location, requiring deletion and re-creation of the existing CloudFormation stack. However, CloudFormation reports that it could not delete the stack cleanly. What is the MOST likely cause, and how can the DevOps engineer mitigate this issue for this and future versions of the website?
options: A. Deletion has failed because the S3 bucket has an active website configuration. Modify the CloudFormation template to remove the WebsiteConfiguration property from the S3 bucket resource.
B. Deletion has failed because the S3 bucket is not empty. Modify the custom resource's AWS Lambda function code to recursively empty the bucket when RequestType is Delete.
C. Deletion has failed because the custom resource does not define a deletion policy. Add a DeletionPolicy property to the custom resource definition with a value of RemoveOnDeletion.
D. Deletion has failed because the S3 bucket is not empty. Modify the S3 bucket resource in the CloudFormation template to add a DeletionPolicy property with a value of Empty.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 buckets must be empty before CloudFormation can delete them. Because the custom resource populated the bucket with website content, its AWS Lambda provider should handle RequestType Delete by recursively removing the bucket objects, allowing the bucket and stack deletion to complete.
learnMore: CloudFormation custom resource request and response reference

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer launches an Amazon EC2 instance with public IP addresses in a public subnet to run an application. A user data script retrieves the application artifacts and installs them on the instances at launch. A change in the application's security classification now requires the instances to operate with no internet access. Although the instances launch successfully and appear healthy, the application does not seem to be installed. Which of the following would successfully install the application while meeting the new requirement?
options: A. Launch the instances in a public subnet with Elastic IP addresses attached. Once the application is installed and running, run a script to disassociate the Elastic IP addresses afterwards.
B. Set up a NAT gateway. Deploy the EC2 instances to a private subnet. Update the private subnet's route table to use the NAT gateway as the default route.

C. Publish the application artifacts to an Amazon S3 bucket and create a VPC endpoint for S3. Assign an IAM instance profile to the EC2 instances so they can read the application artifacts from the S3 bucket.
D. Create a security group for the application instances and allow only outbound traffic to the artifact repository. Remove the security group rule once the install is complete.
questions.explanation: Publishing the artifacts in Amazon S3 and accessing them through an S3 VPC endpoint lets the instances retrieve the required files privately, without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device. An IAM instance profile grants the EC2 instances the permissions needed to read the S3 artifacts.

Gateway endpoints

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A DevOps engineer is working on a project hosted on Amazon Linux that has failed a security review. Question 218 / Security and Compliance A DevOps engineer is working on a project hosted on Amazon Linux that has failed a security review. The DevOps manager has been asked to review the company’s buildspec.yaml file for an AWS CodeBuild project and recommend improvements. The buildspec.yaml file is configured as follows: What changes should be recommended to meet AWS security best practices? Choose three
options: A. Add a post-build command to remove the temporary files from the container before termination to ensure they cannot be seen by other CodeBuild users.
B. Update the CodeBuild project role with the necessary permissions and then remove the AWS credentials from the environment variable.
C. Store the DB_PASSWORD as a SecureString value in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and then remove the DB_PASSWORD from the environment variables.
D. Move the environment variables to the ‘db-deploy-bucket’ Amazon S3 bucket, add a prebuild stage to download, then export the variables.
E. Use AWS Systems Manager run command versus scp and ssh commands directly to the instance.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild should use its IAM service role with least-privilege permissions instead of plaintext, long-term AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY values. Sensitive database credentials should be stored as encrypted Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString values rather than plaintext build environment variables. AWS Systems Manager Run Command provides authenticated, auditable remote management of managed instances and avoids distributing and using an SSH private key for direct scp and ssh access.
learnMore: Build specification reference for CodeBuild

questions.questionText: A company is building a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 Linux instances. The application needs monitoring for custom performance metrics. The company must collect metrics for API response times and database query latency across multiple instances. Which solution will create the custom metrics with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the instances. Configure the agent to collect the custom metrics. Instrument the application to send the metrics to the agent.
B. Use Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus to scrape the custom metrics from the application. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to forward the metrics to CloudWatch.

C. Create a custom AWS Lambda function that polls the application endpoints and database at regular intervals. Program the Lambda function to calculate the custom metrics and to send the metrics to Amazon CloudWatch by using PutMetricData API calls.
D. Implement custom logging in the application code to record the custom metrics. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to extract and analyze the metrics.
questions.explanation: The Amazon CloudWatch agent can receive custom application metrics through the StatsD protocol on Linux and publish them to CloudWatch. Configuring the agent on each instance and instrumenting the application to send those metrics provides direct, managed custom-metric collection without operating a Prometheus deployment, building a polling and PutMetricData Lambda workflow, or deriving metrics from logs.
learnMore: Retrieve custom metrics with StatsD - Amazon CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A company sells products through an ecommerce web application. It needs a dashboard that displays a pie chart of product transaction details. The company wants to integrate the dashboard with its existing Amazon CloudWatch dashboards. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Update the ecommerce application to emit a JSON object to a CloudWatch log group for each processed transaction. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query the log group and to visualize the results in a pie chart format. Attach the results to the desired CloudWatch dashboard.

B. Update the ecommerce application to emit a JSON object to an Amazon S3 bucket for each processed transaction. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket and to visualize the results in a pie chart format. Export the results from Athena. Attach the results to the desired CloudWatch dashboard.

C. Update the ecommerce application to use AWS X-Ray for instrumentation. Create a new X-Ray subsegment. Add an annotation for each processed transaction. Use X-Ray traces to query the data and to visualize the results in a pie chart format. Attach the results to the desired CloudWatch dashboard.

D. Update the ecommerce application to emit a JSON object to a CloudWatch log group for each processed transaction. Create an AWS Lambda function to aggregate and write the results to Amazon DynamoDB. Create a Lambda subscription filter for the log file. Attach the results to the desired CloudWatch dashboard.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs Insights can query and aggregate structured JSON events in a CloudWatch log group, visualize grouped results as a pie chart, and display the query in a CloudWatch dashboard. Using it directly avoids the additional infrastructure and operational overhead of S3/Athena, X-Ray tracing, or Lambda and DynamoDB.
learnMore: Tutorial: Run a query that produces a visualization grouped by log fields
Dashboard Body Structure and Syntax

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company has multiple AWS accounts and uses AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On), integrated with AW… Question 221 / Security and Compliance A company has multiple AWS accounts and uses AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On), integrated with AWS Toolkit for Microsoft Azure DevOps. The attributes-for-access-control feature is enabled in IAM Identity Center. The attribute-mapping list has two entries: the department key maps to $\{path:enterprise.department\}, and the costCenter key maps to $\{path:enterprise.costCenter\}. All existing Amazon EC2 instances have a department tag corresponding to one of three company departments (d1, d2, d3). A DevOps engineer must create policies using matching attributes. The policies must minimize administrative effort and allow each Azure AD user to access only the EC2 instances tagged with that user’s respective department name. Which condition key should the DevOps engineer include in the custom permissions policies to meet these requirements?
options: A.
B.
C.
D.
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center passes configured access-control attributes as session tags, which policies reference with aws:PrincipalTag/department. An EC2 ABAC policy can compare each instance’s department tag using ec2:ResourceTag/department to ${aws:PrincipalTag/department}. This grants access only when the resource’s department matches the authenticated user’s mapped department.
learnMore: Create permission policies for ABAC in IAM Identity Center
Select your attributes for access control

questions.questionText: A developer is building a proof of concept for a new software as a service (SaaS) application. The application resides in a shared development AWS account that belongs to an organization in AWS Organizations. The developer must create service-linked IAM roles for the AWS services being evaluated for the proof of concept. The solution must allow the developer to create and configure only the service-linked roles. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM user for the developer in the organization's management account. Configure a cross-account role in the development account for the developer to use. Limit the scope of the cross-account role to common services.
B. Add the developer to an IAM group. Attach the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the IAM group. Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the user account.
C. Add an SCP to the development account in Organizations. Configure the SCP with a Deny rule for iam:* to limit the developer's access.

D. Create an IAM role that has the necessary IAM access to allow the developer to create policies and roles. Create and attach a permissions boundary to the role. Grant the developer access to assume the role.
questions.explanation: A dedicated IAM role that the developer can assume can be granted only the IAM permissions required for the delegated role-management tasks. A permissions boundary limits the maximum permissions that the role can exercise, preventing delegation from becoming unrestricted IAM administration. IAM permissions boundaries are designed to support delegation of permissions-management tasks. Service-linked roles are owned and controlled by their linked AWS services; their permissions cannot be modified directly in IAM, so access should be restricted to the applicable service-linked-role operations and resources.
learnMore: Create a service-linked role
Permissions boundaries for IAM entities

questions.questionText: A company operates an application that uses an Amazon S3 bucket for image storage. A DevOps engineer must implement a multi-Region strategy for the objects stored in the S3 bucket. The company must be able to fail over to an S3 bucket in a different AWS Region. Whenever an image is added to either S3 bucket, it must replicate to the other S3 bucket within 15 minutes. The DevOps engineer enables two-way replication between the S3 buckets. Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take next to satisfy the requirements? Choose three
options: A. Enable S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) on each replication rule.
B. Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point in an active-passive configuration.
C. Call the SubmitMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes operation in the AWS API when the company needs to fail over to the S3 bucket in the other Region.
D. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on both S3 buckets.
E. Configure a routing control in Amazon Route 53 Recovery Controller. Add the S3 buckets in an active-passive configuration.
questions.explanation: S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) provides an SLA-backed 15-minute replication target, so it must be enabled for each directional replication rule. An Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Point configured active-passive directs requests to the active bucket and supports disaster-recovery failover. SubmitMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes changes the Multi-Region Access Point route states between active and passive to initiate that failover.
learnMore: Replicating objects within and across Regions

questions.questionText: A developer uses the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) to build a prototype for an AWS Lambda function. The AWS SAM template includes an AWS::Serverless::Function resource whose CodeUri property points to an Amazon S3 location. Before creating a CI/CD pipeline, the developer needs to identify the correct deployment commands. The developer creates a Lambda function code archive named package.zip, uploads the .zip archive to the S3 location specified by CodeUri, and runs sam deploy to deploy the Lambda function. The developer updates the Lambda function code and repeats the same deployment steps for the new Lambda function version. The sam deploy command fails with a no-changes-to-deploy error. Which solutions will deploy the new version? Choose two
options: A. Use the aws cloudformation update-stack command instead of the sam deploy command.
B. Use the aws cloudformation update-stack-instances command instead of the sam deploy command.
C. Update the CodeUri property to reference the local application code folder. Use the sam deploy command.
D. Update the CodeUri property to reference the local application code folder. Use the aws cloudformation create-change-set command and the aws cloudformation execute-change-set command.
E. Update the CodeUri property to reference the local application code folder. Use the aws cloudformation package command and the aws cloudformation deploy command.
questions.explanation: Replacing an object at the same S3 URI does not change the CloudFormation template, so it does not create a deployment update. With a local CodeUri, sam deploy uploads the local artifact and updates the template to reference the uploaded artifact location. aws cloudformation package likewise uploads local artifacts and replaces the local CodeUri with an S3 location in the packaged template; aws cloudformation deploy can then deploy the changed template.
learnMore: How AWS SAM uploads local files at deployment
package — AWS CLI Command Reference

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A DevOps engineer has implemented a CI/CD pipeline that deploys an AWS CloudFormation template to provision a… Question 225 / SDLC Automation A DevOps engineer has implemented a CI/CD pipeline that deploys an AWS CloudFormation template to provision a web application. The web application includes an Application Load Balancer (ALB), a target group, a launch template that uses an Amazon Linux 2 AMI, an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances, a security group, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The launch template contains user data that defines a script to install and start the application. The initial application deployment succeeded. The DevOps engineer changed the user data to update the application version. The CI/CD pipeline deployed a new version of the template. However, the ALB health checks are now failing, and they have marked every target unhealthy. During the investigation, the DevOps engineer observes that the CloudFormation stack status is UPDATE_COMPLETE. However, after connecting to an EC2 instance and checking /var/log/messages, the DevOps engineer finds that the Apache web server did not start successfully because of a configuration error. How can the DevOps engineer ensure that the CloudFormation deployment fails if the user data does not finish running successfully?
options: A. Use the cfn-signal helper script to signal success or failure to CloudFormation. Use the WaitOnResourceSignals update policy within the CloudFormation template. Set an appropriate timeout for the update policy.

B. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the UnhealthyHostCount metric. Include an appropriate alarm threshold for the target group. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target to signal success or failure to CloudFormation.

C. Create a lifecycle hook on the Auto Scaling group by using the AWS::AutoScaling::LifecycleHook resource. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target to signal success or failure to CloudFormation. Set an appropriate timeout on the lifecycle hook.

D. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the cloud-init logs. Create a subscription filter that includes an AWS Lambda function with an appropriate invocation timeout. Configure the Lambda function to use the SignalResource API operation to signal success or failure to CloudFormation.
questions.explanation: The cfn-signal helper can send CloudFormation the success or failure result of the user-data bootstrap process. For an Auto Scaling group rolling update, WaitOnResourceSignals: true causes CloudFormation to wait up to the configured PauseTime for the required valid success signals. A failure signal, or failure to receive the required signals before that timeout, causes the stack update to fail.
learnMore: UpdatePolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation
cfn-signal - AWS CloudFormation

questions.questionText: The security team relies on AWS CloudTrail to identify sensitive security issues in the company’s AWS account. The DevOps engineer requires a solution that automatically remediates CloudTrail being disabled in an AWS account. Which solution provides the LEAST downtime for CloudTrail log deliveries?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for the CloudTrail StopLogging event. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on the ARN of the resource in which StopLogging was called. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge rule.

B. Deploy the AWS-managed CloudTrail-enabled AWS Config rule, set with a periodic interval of 1 hour. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for AWS Config rules compliance change. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on the ARN of the resource in which StopLogging was called. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge rule.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for a scheduled event every 5 minutes. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on a CloudTrail trail in the AWS account. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge rule.

D. Launch a t2.nano instance with a script running every 5 minutes that uses the AWS SDK to query CloudTrail in the current account. If the CloudTrail trail is disabled, have the script re-enable the trail.
questions.explanation: The CloudTrail StopLogging API suspends AWS API-call recording and log-file delivery for the specified trail. An Amazon EventBridge rule matching that API call can immediately invoke a Lambda function to call StartLogging for the affected trail, minimizing the interruption without waiting for a scheduled check or periodic AWS Config evaluation.
learnMore: StopLogging - AWS CloudTrail API Reference

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company uses AWS CodeArtifact as a centralized store for Python packages. Question 227 / Security and Compliance A company uses AWS CodeArtifact as a centralized store for Python packages. The CodeArtifact repository has the following repository policy configured: A development team is creating a new project in an account that belongs to an AWS Organizations organization. The team needs to use a Python library that is already stored in the organization's CodeArtifact repository. It uses AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to build the new application. The CodeBuild job used to build the application is configured to run in a VPC. Due to compliance requirements, the VPC has no internet connectivity. The development team creates the VPC endpoints for CodeArtifact and updates the CodeBuild buildspec.yaml file. However, the team cannot download the Python library from the repository. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to allow the development team to use CodeArtifact? Choose two
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint. Update the route tables for the subnets that are running the CodeBuild job.
B. Update the repository policy’s Principal statement to include the ARN of the role that the CodeBuild project uses.
C. Share the CodeArtifact repository with the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
D. Update the role that the CodeBuild project uses so that the role has sufficient permissions to use the CodeArtifact repository.
E. Specify the account that hosts the repository as the delegated administrator for CodeArtifact in the organization.
questions.explanation: The organization-based repository policy already permits principals from the specified AWS Organization, but a principal in another account must also be allowed by an identity-based policy; therefore, the CodeBuild project role needs sufficient CodeArtifact permissions. The expected isolated-VPC configuration also includes an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint associated with the route tables used by the CodeBuild subnets, because CodeArtifact package retrieval can require access to S3-backed package assets. AWS currently documents an exception for Python and Swift packages, which do not require the S3 gateway endpoint, so the Python-specific detail makes this item imperfectly aligned with current documentation.
learnMore: Create the Amazon S3 gateway endpoint - CodeArtifact
Repository policies - CodeArtifact

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodeArtifact as a centralized store for Python packages. The CodeArtifact repository has the following repository policy configured: A development team is creating a new project in an account that belongs to an AWS Organizations organization. The team needs to use a Python library that is already stored in the organization's CodeArtifact repository. It uses AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to build the new application. The CodeBuild job used to build the application is configured to run in a VPC. Due to compliance requirements, the VPC has no internet connectivity. The development team creates the VPC endpoints for CodeArtifact and updates the CodeBuild buildspec.yaml file. However, the team cannot download the Python library from the repository. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to allow the development team to use CodeArtifact? Choose two
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint. Update the route tables for the subnets that are running the CodeBuild job.
B. Update the repository policy’s Principal statement to include the ARN of the role that the CodeBuild project uses.
C. Share the CodeArtifact repository with the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
D. Update the role that the CodeBuild project uses so that the role has sufficient permissions to use the CodeArtifact repository.
E. Specify the account that hosts the repository as the delegated administrator for CodeArtifact in the organization.
questions.explanation: The organization-based repository policy already permits principals from the specified AWS Organization, but a principal in another account must also be allowed by an identity-based policy; therefore, the CodeBuild project role needs sufficient CodeArtifact permissions. The expected isolated-VPC configuration also includes an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint associated with the route tables used by the CodeBuild subnets, because CodeArtifact package retrieval can require access to S3-backed package assets. AWS currently documents an exception for Python and Swift packages, which do not require the S3 gateway endpoint, so the Python-specific detail makes this item imperfectly aligned with current documentation.
learnMore: Create the Amazon S3 gateway endpoint - CodeArtifact
Repository policies - CodeArtifact

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations and AWS Control Tower to manage its multi-account environment. The company needs to deploy standardized security controls and compliance policies throughout all of its AWS accounts and AWS Regions. Any modifications to these controls must automatically be applied to every account at the same time. The required security controls and compliance policies are defined in the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) as a security controls construct. Which solution will deploy these controls across every account and Region with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an AWS CDK app that includes an AWS CloudFormation StackSets construct. Configure the StackSets construct to use the security controls construct as its template. Specify the target accounts and Regions. Create automation to deploy the CDK app to create and manage the CloudFormation stack set.

B. Create an AWS CDK app that synthesizes an AWS CloudFormation template from the security controls construct. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update a CloudFormation stack set when changes are made to the security controls construct.

C. Convert the security controls construct to an AWS CloudFormation macro. Create a CloudFormation stack set that references the macro and deploys the macro to all target accounts. Use Organizations to automatically add new accounts to the stack set’s list of target accounts.

D. Use AWS Control Tower to create a customized landing zone that includes configurations from the security controls construct. Configure AWS Control Tower to automatically enroll new accounts and to apply the landing zone template.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation StackSets deploy the same CloudFormation template to specified AWS accounts and Regions, and an update to a StackSet updates its associated stack instances. When used with AWS Organizations service-managed permissions, StackSets can target organizational accounts or OUs without manually managing per-account deployment roles. A CDK app can define and manage the StackSet from the security-controls construct, allowing one managed deployment path to propagate control changes consistently.
learnMore: Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions

questions.questionText: A company has deployed a new REST API using Amazon API Gateway. The company uses the API to access confidential data. The API must be accessible only from specific VPCs within the company. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create and attach a resource policy to the API Gateway API. Configure the resource policy to allow only the specific VPC IDs.
B. Add a security group to the API Gateway API. Configure the inbound rules to allow only the specific VPC IP address ranges.
C. Create and attach an IAM role to the API Gateway API. Configure the IAM role to allow only the specific VPC IDs.
D. Add an ACL to the API Gateway API. Configure the outbound rules to allow only the specific VPC IP address ranges.
questions.explanation: An API Gateway resource policy can restrict REST API invocation to specified VPCs by using the aws:SourceVpc condition. API Gateway does not use directly attached security groups or network ACLs for this control, and IAM roles govern identities rather than limiting access by VPC ID.
learnMore: Control access to a REST API with API Gateway resource policies

questions.questionText: A company stores 100 GB of log data in .csv format in an Amazon S3 bucket. SQL developers need to query this data and create graphs to visualize it. The SQL developers also require an efficient, automated method to store metadata from the .csv file. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the LEAST effort? Choose three
options: A. Filter the data through AWS X-Ray to visualize the data.
B. Filter the data through Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
C. Query the data with Amazon Athena.
D. Query the data with Amazon Redshift.
E. Use the AWS Glue Data Catalog as the persistent metadata store.
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena runs standard SQL queries directly against data in Amazon S3 without infrastructure to manage. Amazon QuickSight creates graphical data visualizations. The AWS Glue Data Catalog is the persistent metadata store, and AWS Glue crawlers can automatically infer CSV schemas and populate it with table metadata.
learnMore: Adding visuals to QuickSight analyses

questions.questionText: A company operates a fleet of Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS account. The company uses an AWS Systems Manager Automation task across those EC2 instances. In the latest patch cycle, several EC2 instances entered an error state because they did not have enough available disk space. A DevOps engineer must ensure that the EC2 instances have sufficient free disk space during future patching operations. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Ensure that the Amazon CloudWatch agent is installed on all EC2 instances.
B. Create a cron job that is installed on each EC2 instance to periodically delete temporary files.

C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch log group for the EC2 instances. Configure a cron job that is installed on each EC2 instance to write the available disk space to a CloudWatch log stream for the relevant EC2 instance.
D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor available disk space on all EC2 instances. Add the alarm as a safety control to the Systems Manager Automation task.
E. Create an AWS Lambda function to periodically check for sufficient available disk space on all EC2 instances by evaluating each EC2 instance's respective Amazon CloudWatch log stream.
questions.explanation: The Amazon CloudWatch agent collects Linux disk metrics, including disk_free and disk_used_percent, which make available disk capacity observable for each instance. A CloudWatch alarm can evaluate those metrics and be applied to a Systems Manager Automation execution as an alarm control; if the alarm enters the ALARM state, Systems Manager cancels the automation. This prevents the patch process from continuing when the configured disk-space threshold is not met.
learnMore: Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent
Run an automated operation powered by Systems Manager Automation
