questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is working on a data-archival project that requires migrating on-premises data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The DevOps engineer creates a script that incrementally archives on-premises data older than 1 month to Amazon S3. Data transferred to Amazon S3 is removed from the on-premises location. The script uses the S3 PutObject operation. During a code review, the DevOps engineer realizes that the script does not confirm whether the data was copied successfully to Amazon S3. The DevOps engineer must modify the script to ensure that data is not corrupted in transit. The script must use MD5 checksums to validate data integrity before deleting the on-premises data. Which solutions for the script meet these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Check the returned response for the VersionId. Compare the returned VersionId against the MD5 checksum.
B. Include the MD5 checksum within the Content-MD5 parameter. Check the operation call’s return status to find out if an error was returned.
C. Include the checksum digest within the tagging parameter as a URL query parameter.
D. Check the returned response for the ETag. Compare the returned ETag against the MD5 checksum.
E. Include the checksum digest within the Metadata parameter as a name-value pair. After upload, use the S3 HeadObject operation to retrieve metadata from the object.
questions.explanation: The Content-MD5 parameter supplies a Base64-encoded MD5 digest that Amazon S3 uses as an end-to-end integrity check; S3 rejects the upload if the received payload does not match. For applicable single-part PutObject uploads, the returned ETag is the MD5 digest of the object data, so it can be compared with the locally calculated MD5 checksum.
learnMore: PutObject - Amazon S3 API Reference
Checking object integrity for data uploads in Amazon S3

questions.questionText: A company deploys an application to Amazon EC2 instances. The application runs Amazon Linux 2 and uses AWS CodeDeploy. The application has the following code-repository file structure: The files section of the appspec.yml file contains the following: What will be the deployment result for the config.txt file?
options: A. The config.txt file will be deployed to only /var/www/html/config/config.txt.
B. The config.txt file will be deployed to /usr/local/src/config.txt and to /var/www/html/config/config.txt.
C. The config.txt file will be deployed to only /usr/local/src/config.txt.
D. The config.txt file will be deployed to /usr/local/src/config.txt and to /var/www/html/application/web/config.txt.
questions.explanation: The explicit file mapping deploys config/config.txt to /usr/local/src/config.txt. The source: / mapping copies the complete CodeDeploy revision bundle to /var/www/html while preserving its relative directory structure, which also deploys the file to /var/www/html/config/config.txt.
learnMore: AppSpec 'files' section (EC2/On-Premises deployments only)

questions.questionText: A company runs an application in two AWS Regions. The application currently uses an Amazon S3 bucket in the primary Region for data storage. A DevOps engineer must ensure that the application is highly available across both Regions. The engineer has created a new S3 bucket in the secondary Region. Both S3 buckets must contain all existing and future objects. The application must be able to fail over between the Regions without data loss. Which combination of steps satisfies these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency? Choose three
options: A. Create a new IAM role that allows the Amazon S3 and S3 Batch Operations service principals to assume the role that has the necessary permissions for S3 replication.
B. Create a new IAM role that allows the AWS Batch service principal to assume the role that has the necessary permissions for S3 replication.
C. Create an S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) rule on the source S3 bucket. Configure the rule to use the IAM role for Amazon S3 to replicate to the target S3 bucket.
D. Create a two-way replication rule on the source S3 bucket. Configure the rule to use the IAM role for Amazon S3 to replicate to the target S3 bucket.

E. Create an AWS Batch job that has an AWS Fargate orchestration type. Configure the job to use the IAM role for AWS Batch. Specify a Bash command to use the AWS CLI to synchronize the contents of the source S3 bucket and the target S3 bucket
questions.explanation: S3 Batch Replication performs the on-demand backfill of objects that existed before replication was configured, while two-way S3 replication keeps objects synchronized when writes occur in either Regional bucket during failover. The IAM role must trust Amazon S3 for live replication and S3 Batch Operations for the Batch Replication job, and must grant the required permissions on both buckets.
learnMore: Replicating existing objects with Batch Replication
Create two-way replication rules for your Multi-Region Access Point

questions.questionText: A company regularly creates Docker images for an application and stores them in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The company creates both tagged and untagged images. The company needs a solution that automatically deletes images that have not been updated for a long time and are not used frequently. The solution must retain at least a specified number of images. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies on the ECR repository to automatically delete images based on image age or the absence of tags on the image.
B. Use Amazon ECR lifecycle policies to delete images based on age or the number of images that need to be to retained in the repository.
C. Configure an AWS Lambda function to run a schedule to delete images based on age or the number of images that need to be retained in the repository.
D. Use AWS Systems Manager to run a script by using the aws:executeScript action to automatically delete images based on image age or the absence of tags on the image.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR lifecycle policies natively automate image expiration for tagged, untagged, or all images. Policy rules can expire images by age and can use an image-count threshold that retains the configured number of images, avoiding custom scheduled code or scripts.
learnMore: Automate the cleanup of images by using lifecycle policies in Amazon ECR
Lifecycle policy properties in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A company stores sensitive API keys in AWS Secrets Manager for use by an AWS Lambda function. Each time the Lambda function is invoked, it retrieves the API keys and calls an external service. The Secrets Manager secret is encrypted with the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. A DevOps engineer must update the infrastructure so that only the Lambda function’s execution role can access the values in Secrets Manager. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Update the default KMS key for Secrets Manager to allow only the Lambda function’s execution role to decrypt
B. Create a KMS customer managed key that trusts Secrets Manager and allows the Lambda function's execution role to decrypt. Update Secrets Manager to use the new customer managed key
C. Create a KMS customer managed key that trusts Secrets Manager and allows the account's root principal to decrypt. Update Secrets Manager to use the new customer managed key
D. Ensure that the Lambda function’s execution role has the KMS permissions scoped on the resource level. Configure the permissions so that the KMS key can encrypt the Secrets Manager secret
E. Remove all KMS permissions from the Lambda function’s execution role
questions.explanation: The AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager has a service-defined key policy that cannot be changed. A customer managed KMS key permits a restrictive key policy that authorizes Secrets Manager and grants kms:Decrypt only to the Lambda execution role. Removing separate KMS permissions from the Lambda role prevents broader or redundant IAM grants while the narrowly scoped customer-managed-key policy supplies the required decrypt authorization.
learnMore: Secret encryption and decryption in AWS Secrets Manager
Change a key policy - AWS Key Management Service

questions.questionText: A company intends to use AWS Systems Manager documents to bootstrap physical laptops for developers. The bootstrap code is stored in GitHub. A DevOps engineer has already created a Systems Manager activation, installed the Systems Manager agent using the registration code, and installed an activation ID on all the laptops. Which set of steps should be performed next?
options: A. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the AWS-RunShellScript command to copy the files from GitHub to Amazon S3, then use the aws-downloadContent plugin with a sourceType of S3.
B. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the aws-configurePackage plugin with an install action and point to the Git repository.
C. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the aws-downloadContent plugin with a sourceType of GitHub and sourceInfo with the repository details.
D. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the aws:softwareInventory plugin and run the script from the Git repository.
questions.explanation: The aws:downloadContent Systems Manager document plugin downloads scripts and SSM documents from remote locations, including GitHub. With sourceType set to GitHub, sourceInfo supplies the GitHub repository details needed to retrieve the bootstrap content.
learnMore: Command document plugin reference - AWS Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A company has several AWS accounts in an AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled. The company’s DevOps administrator must improve security throughout all of the company’s AWS accounts. The administrator must identify the most frequently used users and roles across every account. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create a new organization trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure the trail to send log events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule for the userIdentity.arn log field. View the results in CloudWatch Contributor Insights.

B. Create an unused access analysis for the organization by using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer. Review the analyzer results and determine if each finding has the intended level of permissions required for the workload.

C. Create a new organization trail in AWS CloudTrail. Create a table in Amazon Athena that uses partition projection. Load the Athena table with CloudTrail data. Query the Athena table to find the top users and roles.
D. Generate a Service access report for each account by using Organizations. From the results, pull the last accessed date and last accessed by account fields to find the top users and roles.
questions.explanation: An AWS CloudTrail organization trail centralizes events from the organization’s management and member accounts and can deliver them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. A CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule can analyze CloudTrail JSON logs by the high-cardinality userIdentity.arn field and rank the identities generating the most activity, which identifies the top users and roles without maintaining an Athena data-query workflow.
learnMore: CloudTrail concepts — Organization trails
Create a Contributor Insights rule in CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A healthcare services company is worried about increasing software-licensing costs for an application that monitors patient wellness. The company wants to establish an audit process to ensure that the application runs only on Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts. A DevOps engineer must create a workflow that audits the application for compliance. Which steps should the engineer take to satisfy this requirement with the LEAST administrative overhead?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager Configuration Compliance. Use calls to the put-compliance-items API action to scan and build a database of noncompliant EC2 instances based on their host placement configuration. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store these instance IDs for fast access. Generate a report through Systems Manager by calling the list-compliance-summaries API action.

B. Use custom Java code running on an EC2 instance. Set up EC2 Auto Scaling for the instance depending on the number of instances to be checked. Send the list of noncompliant EC2 instance IDs to an Amazon SQS queue. Set up another worker instance to process instance IDs from the SQS queue and write them to Amazon DynamoDUse an AWS Lambda function to terminate noncompliant instance IDs obtained from the queue, and send them to an Amazon SNS email topic for distribution.

C. Use AWS Config. Identify all EC2 instances to be audited by enabling Config Recording on all Amazon EC2 resources for the region. Create a custom AWS Config rule that triggers an AWS Lambda function by using the "config-rule-change -triggered" blueprint. Modify the Lambda evaluateCompliance() function to verify host placement to return a NON_COMPLIANT result if the instance is not running on an EC2 Dedicated Host. Use the AWS Config report to address noncompliant instances.

D. Use AWS CloudTrail. Identify all EC2 instances to be audited by analyzing all calls to the EC2 RunCommand API action. Invoke an AWS Lambda function that analyzes the host placement of the instance. Store the EC2 instance ID of noncompliant resources in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Generate a report by querying the RDS instance and exporting the query results to a CSV text file.
questions.explanation: AWS Config records EC2 resource configuration and supports change-triggered custom rules that invoke AWS Lambda to evaluate AWS::EC2::Instance resources. The rule can evaluate the instance’s host placement and report any instance not running on an EC2 Dedicated Host as NON_COMPLIANT; AWS Config retains and reports the resulting compliance status. This avoids operating custom polling infrastructure, databases, queues, and report-generation workflows. AWS also documents AWS Config as a source for Dedicated Host and instance configuration data used for license reporting.
learnMore: Track Amazon EC2 Dedicated Host configuration changes using AWS Config
Creating AWS Config Custom Lambda Rules

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company has an AWS account named PipelineAccount. Question 245 / Security and Compliance A company has an AWS account named PipelineAccount. This account manages a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. It uses an IAM role named CodePipeline_Service_Role and creates an artifact that is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses a customer managed AWS KMS key to encrypt objects in the S3 bucket. A DevOps engineer wants to configure the pipeline to use an AWS CodeDeploy application in an AWS account named CodeDeployAccount to deploy the produced artifact. The DevOps engineer updates the KMS key policy to give the CodeDeployAccount account permission to use the key. The DevOps engineer configures an IAM role named DevOps_Role in the CodeDeployAccount account that can access the CodeDeploy resources required by the pipeline. The DevOps engineer updates an Amazon EC2 instance role operating in the CodeDeployAccount account to allow access to the S3 bucket and the KMS key in the PipelineAccount account. Which additional steps will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the CodeDeployAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the PipelineAccount account to assume the role. Update the CodePipeline_Service_Role IAM role to grant permission to assume the DevOps_Role role.

B. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the CodeDeployAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the PipelineAccount account to assume the role. Update the DevOps_Role IAM role to grant permission to assume CodePipelfne_Service_Role role.

C. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the PipelineAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the PipelineAccount account to assume the role. Update the CodePipeline_Service_Role IAM to grant permission to assume the DevOps_Role role.

D. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the CodeDeployAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the CodeDeployAccount account to assume the role. Update the CodePipeline_Service_Role IAM role to grant permission to assume the DevOps_Role role.
questions.explanation: For a pipeline in one account to use CodeDeploy resources in another account, the artifact bucket policy must allow the target account to access the artifacts. The cross-account role in the CodeDeploy account must trust the CodePipeline service role in the pipeline account, and that service role needs sts:AssumeRole permission on the cross-account role. This gives the assumed DevOps_Role access to the CodeDeploy resources and artifact bucket while the EC2 instance role retrieves and decrypts the deployment artifact.

questions.questionText: A company is organized into teams. Every team has an AWS account, and all accounts belong to one AWS Organizations organization. Each team must retain complete administrative permissions in its AWS account. Each team must also be able to use only AWS services that the company has approved. AWS services receive approval through a request-and-approval process. How should a DevOps engineer configure the accounts to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to provision IAM policies in each account to deny access to restricted AWS services. In each account, configure AWS Config rules that ensure that the policies are attached to IAM principals in the account.

B. Use AWS Control Tower to provision the accounts into OUs within the organization. Configure AWS Control Tower to enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure IAM Identity Center to provide administrative access. Include deny policies on user roles for restricted AWS services.
C. Place all the accounts under a new top-level OU within the organization. Create an SCP that denies access to restricted AWS services. Attach the SCP to the OU.
D. Create an SCP that allows access to only approved AWS services. Attach the SCP to the root OU of the organization. Remove the FullAWSAccess SCP from the root OU of the organization.
questions.explanation: Service control policies (SCPs) define the maximum permissions available to identities in affected AWS accounts, including administrators. Replacing the default FullAWSAccess SCP at the organization root with an SCP that explicitly allows only approved services implements an organization-wide allow list; services not explicitly allowed are unavailable until the policy is updated after approval.
learnMore: SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations
Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: A company needs to proactively monitor and respond to AWS service issues that could affect an application. The company must correlate AWS Health events with application performance metrics and configure automated alerts. The solution must enable the company to archive events, test the application's latency under different scenarios, and create custom metrics. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CloudTrail to log all AWS Health events. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs and to correlate the logs with application metrics stored in Amazon Timestream for LiveAnalytics. Set up AWS Chatbot for real-time notifications.

B. Use Amazon EventBridge to route AWS Health events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a metric filter for AWS Health events. Create custom metrics in CloudWatch that are based on application performance data. Set up CloudWatch alarms that correlate AWS Health events with the custom metrics.

C. Configure the AWS Health Dashboard to send notifications to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Use AWS Lambda to correlate the notifications with metrics and to update custom metrics in Amazon CloudWatch. Set up CloudWatch alarms for the custom metrics. Use AWS Systems Manager for automated remediation.

D. Configure AWS X-Ray to trace AWS Health events and application performance. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the correlations between events and metrics. Use Amazon GuardDuty to detect anomalies in the application's behavior and to provide alerts.
questions.explanation: Amazon EventBridge can receive AWS Health events and route them to CloudWatch Logs for retention. CloudWatch Logs metric filters turn matching Health log events into CloudWatch metrics, while CloudWatch custom metrics represent application performance data. CloudWatch alarms can evaluate the resulting metrics, including metric-math expressions, to alert on the relationship between AWS Health events and application performance. CloudWatch also supports Synthetics canaries for scheduled endpoint and latency testing.
learnMore: Monitoring events in AWS Health with Amazon EventBridge
Creating metrics from log events using filters

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage 10 AWS accounts. All features are enabled, and trusted access for AWS CloudFormation is enabled. A DevOps engineer must use CloudFormation to deploy an IAM role to the Organizations management account and to every member account in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has service-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target.
B. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has service-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target. Deploy a separate CloudFormation stack in the Organizations management account.
C. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has self-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target.
D. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has self-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target. Deploy a separate CloudFormation stack in the Organizations management account.
questions.explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions use AWS Organizations integration and avoid manually creating and managing cross-account IAM roles. Targeting the root organizational unit deploys to all member accounts, but service-managed StackSets do not deploy stacks to the Organizations management account. A separate CloudFormation stack in that account is required.
learnMore: Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions
Prerequisites for using CloudFormation StackSets

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage 10 AWS accounts. All features are enabled, and trusted access for AWS CloudFormation is enabled. A DevOps engineer must use CloudFormation to deploy an IAM role to the Organizations management account and to every member account in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has service-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target.
B. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has service-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target. Deploy a separate CloudFormation stack in the Organizations management account.
C. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has self-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target.
D. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has self-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target. Deploy a separate CloudFormation stack in the Organizations management account.
questions.explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions use AWS Organizations integration and avoid manually creating and managing cross-account IAM roles. Targeting the root organizational unit deploys to all member accounts, but service-managed StackSets do not deploy stacks to the Organizations management account. A separate CloudFormation stack in that account is required.

Prerequisites for using CloudFormation StackSets

questions.questionText: A company has recently migrated its application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that uses Amazon EC2 instances. The company configured the application for automatic scaling based on CPU utilization. The application generates memory errors during heavy loads. It also does not scale out sufficiently to accommodate the increased load. The company must collect and analyze application memory metrics over time. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Attach the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy managed IAM policy to the IAM instance profile that the cluster uses.
B. Attach the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy managed IAM policy to a service account role for the cluster.

C. Collect performance metrics by deploying the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent to the existing EC2 instances in the cluster. Add the agent to the AMI for any new EC2 instances that are added to the cluster.
D. Collect performance logs by deploying the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry collector as a DaemonSet.
E. Analyze the pod_memory_utilization Amazon CloudWatch metric in the ContainerInsights namespace by using the Service dimension.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Container Insights collects EKS workload metrics through the CloudWatch agent. For EC2 worker nodes, the agent requires CloudWatch permissions from the worker-node IAM instance profile, and the agent must be deployed on both current and subsequently added EC2 instances. The pod_memory_utilization metric supports a Service dimension, enabling memory analysis for the application service over time; node_memory_utilization instead measures worker-node memory usage.
learnMore: Container Insights

questions.questionText: A company has configured AWS CodeArtifact repositories with public upstream repositories. The company’s development team uses open-source dependencies from these repositories on the internal network. The security team recently identified a critical vulnerability in the latest version of a package consumed by the development team. The security team has created a patched version to remediate the vulnerability. The company must stop the vulnerable version from being downloaded. The company must also permit the security team to publish the patched version. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Update the status of the affected CodeArtifact package version to unlisted.
B. Update the status of the affected CodeArtifact package version to deleted.
C. Update the status of the affected CodeArtifact package version to archived.
D. Update the CodeArtifact package origin control settings to allow direct publishing and to block upstream operations.
E. Update the CodeArtifact package origin control settings to block direct publishing and to allow upstream operations.
questions.explanation: Deleting the affected package version removes it from the repository, prevents downloads, and allows that version to be republished. CodeArtifact package origin controls must allow direct publishing so the security team can publish the patched package, and must block upstream operations so the vulnerable version cannot be retained again from a public upstream repository. An Unlisted version can still be downloaded, while an Archived version cannot be republished through a package manager because it remains in the repository.
learnMore: Packages overview - CodeArtifact
Editing package origin controls - CodeArtifact

questions.questionText: A company's video-streaming platform usage has grown from 10,000 users per day to 50,000 users per day across multiple countries. The company deploys the streaming platform on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The EKS workload scales to thousands of nodes during peak viewing periods. The company's users report instances of unauthorized logins. Users also report unexpected interruptions and logouts from the platform. The company wants extra security measures for the entire platform. The company also requires a summarized view of resource behaviors and interactions across the company's full AWS environment. The summarized view must display login attempts, API calls, and network traffic. The solution must allow network-traffic analysis while minimizing log-management overhead. The solution must also rapidly investigate any potential malicious behavior associated with the EKS workload. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Enable Amazon GuardDuty for EKS Audit Log Monitoring. Enable AWS CloudTrail logs. Store the EKS audit logs and CloudTrail log files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to create an external table. Use Amazon QuickSight to create a dashboard.
B. Enable Amazon GuardDuty for EKS Audit Log Monitoring. Enable Amazon Detective in the company's AWS account. Enable EKS audit logs from optional source packages in Detective.

C. Enable Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights. Enable AWS CloudTrail logs. Store the EKS audit logs and CloudTrail log files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to create an external table. Use Amazon QuickSight to create a dashboard.
D. Enable Amazon GuardDuty for EKS Audit Log Monitoring. Enable Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights and VPC Flow Logs. Enable AWS CloudTrail logs.
questions.explanation: Amazon Detective automatically aggregates and visualizes login attempts, AWS API calls, VPC network traffic, and GuardDuty findings as a unified behavior graph, avoiding the need to manually enable or store the underlying CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs for this analysis. Its optional EKS audit log data source adds EKS-cluster detail and correlates it with CloudTrail management events and VPC Flow Logs. GuardDuty EKS Audit Log Monitoring analyzes EKS audit activity and produces findings for potential threats, enabling rapid investigation in Detective.

questions.questionText: A company has a 24-hour RPO and a 10-minute RTO for a critical web application running on Amazon EC2 instances. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS account and wants to configure AWS Backup for its AWS environment. A DevOps engineer configures AWS Organizations for AWS Backup and creates a new centralized AWS account to hold the backups. Each EC2 instance has four attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Which solution meets this requirement MOST securely?
options: A. Create encrypted backup vaults and customer managed AWS KMS keys in both accounts. Configure AWS Backup to create full EC2 backups as AMIs. Copy the backups to the centralized vault.
B. Create encrypted vaults in both accounts by using the source account's AWS KMS key. Configure AWS Backup to create EC2 AMIs. Copy the AMIs to the centralized vault.
C. Create backup vaults in both accounts. Use AWS managed keys for encryption. Configure AWS Backup to create EC2 AMIs. Copy the AMIs to the centralized vault.

D. Create encrypted vaults in both accounts. Use a customer managed KMS key in the source account. Use an AWS managed key in the centralized account. Configure AWS Backup to create EC2 AMIs. Copy the AMIs to the centralized vault.
questions.explanation: AWS Backup uses the encryption of the underlying EBS volumes for Amazon EC2 backups. EC2 is not fully managed by AWS Backup for this purpose, so cross-account backup copies cannot use AWS managed KMS keys: their key policies cannot be modified to authorize cross-account access. Customer managed KMS keys in both accounts allow the required key-policy permissions while encrypting the source and centralized backup vaults. An EC2 AMI backup captures the instance and its attached EBS volumes.
learnMore: Encryption for backups in AWS Backup
Creating backup copies across AWS accounts

questions.questionText: A company operates a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The company’s employees access the EC2 instances remotely by using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP). The company needs to collect metrics for the number of RDP sessions that employees initiate each day. Which combination of steps satisfies this requirement? Choose three
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to EC2 Instance State-change Notification events.
B. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Specify the log group as a target for the EventBridge rule.
C. Create a flow log in VPC Flow Logs.
D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Specify the log group as a destination for the flow log.
E. Create a log group metric filter.
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic to and from VPC network interfaces, including RDP traffic on TCP destination port 3389. Publishing the flow log to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group makes the records available to a CloudWatch Logs metric filter, which can match the RDP traffic pattern and increment a metric for daily session counts.

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances span multiple Availability Zones. The application was incorrectly configured in one Availability Zone, causing a partial application outage. A DevOps engineer changed the configuration so that unhealthy EC2 instances in one Availability Zone do not affect healthy EC2 instances in the other Availability Zones. The DevOps engineer must test the application's failover and change where the ALB directs traffic. During failover, the ALB must not send traffic to the Availability Zone in which the failure occurred. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Turn off cross-zone load balancing on the ALB. Use Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to start a zonal shift away from the Availability Zone.
B. Turn off cross-zone load balancing on the ALB’s target group. Use Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to start a zonal shift away from the Availability Zone.
C. Create an Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller resource set that uses the DNS hostname of the ALB. Start a zonal shift for the resource set away from the Availability Zone.
D. Create an Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller resource set that uses the ARN of the ALB’s target group. Create a readiness check that uses the ElbV2TargetGroupsCanServeTraffic rule.
questions.explanation: For an Application Load Balancer, cross-zone load balancing cannot be disabled at the load-balancer level, but it can be explicitly disabled at the target-group level. With cross-zone load balancing off for the target group, each load balancer node routes only to targets in its own Availability Zone. An ARC zonal shift for the ALB shifts traffic away from the impaired Availability Zone, preventing new traffic from being directed there.

questions.questionText: A company operates an application across multiple environments in one AWS account. An AWS CodePipeline pipeline uses a development Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster to test an application image from an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. The pipeline then promotes the image to a production ECS cluster. The company must move the production cluster to a separate AWS account in the same AWS Region. The production cluster must be able to download the images through a private connection. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon ECR VPC endpoints and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint. In the separate AWS account, create an ECR repository. Set the repository policy to allow the production ECS tasks to pull images from the main AWS account. Configure the production ECS task execution role to have permission to download the image from the ECR repository.

B. Set a repository policy on the production ECR repository in the main AWS account. Configure the repository policy to allow the production ECS tasks in the separate AWS account to pull images from the main account. Configure the production ECS task execution role to have permission to download the image from the ECR repository.
C. Configure ECR private image replication in the main AWS account. Activate cross-account replication. Define the destination account ID of the separate AWS account.

D. Use Amazon ECR VPC endpoints and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint. Set a repository policy on the production ECR repository in the main AWS account. Configure the repository policy to allow the production ECS tasks in the separate AWS account to pull images from the main account. Configure the production ECS task execution role to have permission to download the image from the ECR repository.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR repository policies can grant cross-account access to a source repository, while the ECS task execution role needs the relevant ECR permissions to authenticate and retrieve images. For private ECS image pulls, Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints provide private access to the ECR APIs and registry, and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint is required to retrieve the image layers that ECR stores in S3.
learnMore: Private repository policies in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A company hosts an application on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The application's metadata is kept in Amazon S3 and must be retrieved whenever the instance is restarted. The instance must automatically restart or be relaunched if it becomes unresponsive. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed metric. Use the recover action to stop and start the instance. Use an S3 event notification to push the metadata to the instance when the instance is back up and running.
B. Configure AWS OpsWorks, and use the auto healing feature to stop and start the instance. Use a lifecycle event in OpsWorks to pull the metadata from Amazon S3 and update it on the instance.
C. Use EC2 Auto Recovery to automatically stop and start the instance in case of a failure. Use an S3 event notification to push the metadata to the instance when the instance is back up and running.
D. Use AWS CloudFormation to create an EC2 instance that includes the UserData property for the EC2 resource. Add a command in UserData to retrieve the application metadata from Amazon S3.
questions.explanation: AWS OpsWorks Stacks Auto Healing detects an unresponsive managed instance and automatically recovers it by stopping and starting an Amazon EBS-backed instance or replacing an instance-store-backed instance. OpsWorks lifecycle events run associated recipes during instance initialization and configuration, so a recipe can retrieve the required application metadata from Amazon S3 after recovery.

questions.questionText: A company has an on-premises application written in Go. A DevOps engineer needs to migrate the application to AWS. The company's development team wants to support blue/green deployments and conduct A/B testing. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Deploy the application on an Amazon EC2 instance, and create an AMI of the instance. Use the AMI to create an automatic scaling launch configuration that is used in an Auto Scaling group. Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute traffic. When changes are made to the application, a new AMI will be created, which will initiate an EC2 instance refresh.

B. Use Amazon Lightsail to deploy the application. Store the application in a zipped format in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use this zipped version to deploy new versions of the application to Lightsail. Use Lightsail deployment options to manage the deployment.

C. Use AWS CodeArtifact to store the application code. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the application to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute the traffic to the EC2 instances. When making changes to the application, upload a new version to CodeArtifact and create a new CodeDeploy deployment.

D. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to host the application. Store a zipped version of the application in Amazon S3. Use that location to deploy new versions of the application. Use Elastic Beanstalk to manage the deployment options.
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk supports deployment of Go applications from application source bundles and provides managed deployment policies. Its traffic-splitting deployment policy launches new instances and sends a specified percentage of incoming traffic to the new application version during an evaluation period, while the remaining traffic continues to use the existing version. This supports controlled version testing and rollback, alongside blue/green-style deployment workflows.

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy applications to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. In a recent deployment, several EC2 instances did not update successfully. A DevOps engineer needs to investigate the root cause of these failures and identify the specific deployment lifecycle events that had errors. What is the MOST operationally efficient method to access and analyze detailed deployment logs for troubleshooting?
options: A. Use SSH to connect to each EC2 instance that failed to update successfully. Read the logs from the CodeDeploy agent.
B. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to each EC2 instance that failed to update successfully. Read the logs from the CodeDeploy agent.
C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store CodeDeploy logs. Update the appspec.yml file to copy logs to the S3 bucket. Query the S3 bucket by using Amazon Athena
D. Send CodeDeploy agent logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs by using the CloudWatch agent. Analyze the logs by using CloudWatch Logs Insights.
questions.explanation: The CloudWatch agent can send CodeDeploy agent logs from all target instances to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, providing a centralized view rather than requiring access to every failed instance. CloudWatch Logs Insights can then query and analyze those aggregated logs to identify errors in particular deployment lifecycle events.

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company receives reports that its order history page is delayed in showing the processing status of orders. The order-processing system includes an AWS Lambda function that uses reserved concurrency. The Lambda function processes order messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and writes processed orders to an Amazon DynamoDB table. The DynamoDB table has auto scaling enabled for read and write capacity. Which actions should a DevOps engineer take to resolve this delay? Choose two
options: A. Check the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric for the SQS queue. Increase the Lambda function concurrency limit.
B. Check the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metnc for the SQS queue Configure a redrive policy on the SQS queue.
C. Check the NumberOfMessagesSent metric for the SQS queue. Increase the SQS queue visibility timeout.
D. Check the WriteThrottleEvents metric for the DynamoDB table. Increase the maximum write capacity units (WCUs) for the table's scaling policy.
E. Check the Throttles metric for the Lambda function. Increase the Lambda function timeout.
questions.explanation: ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage measures the age of the oldest unprocessed SQS message, so it reveals a queue-processing backlog. A reserved-concurrency setting can limit the number of simultaneous Lambda invocations available to consume that backlog. WriteThrottleEvents indicates DynamoDB writes exceeding provisioned write capacity. DynamoDB auto scaling operates only within its configured minimum and maximum WCU range, so raising the maximum WCU can allow the table to scale high enough to avoid write throttling.
learnMore: Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings
Available CloudWatch metrics for Amazon SQS

questions.questionText: A company runs AWS Storage Gateway in file gateway mode in front of an Amazon S3 bucket that multiple resources use. When business starts in the morning, users cannot see objects that a third party processed the previous evening. A DevOps engineer verifies that the data exists by checking the S3 bucket directly, but it does not appear in Storage Gateway. Which solution makes sure that all updated third-party files are available in the morning?
options: A. Configure a nightly Amazon EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to run the RefreshCache command for Storage Gateway.
B. Instruct the third party to put data into the S3 bucket using AWS Transfer for SFTP.
C. Modify Storage Gateway to run in volume gateway mode.
D. Use S3 Same-Region Replication to replicate any changes made directly in the S3 bucket to Storage Gateway.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway caches its S3 object inventory and does not automatically update that inventory for objects uploaded directly to the bucket outside the gateway workflow. Invoking RefreshCache refreshes the file share’s cached inventory to find added, removed, or replaced S3 objects; a nightly scheduled invocation therefore exposes the third-party updates before users begin work.

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company operates application environments in multiple AWS accounts. Question 264 / Incident and Event Response A company operates application environments in multiple AWS accounts. Each environment account resides in a separate OU in AWS Organizations. A DevOps team manages the application deployment process across these environments. The process uses an AWS CodePipeline pipeline in a Shared Services account. All DevOps team members belong to the same user group and have administrative access to every account through AWS IAM Identity Center. A recent deployment issue in the development environment required the DevOps team to take manual actions. The subsequent deployment to the production environment caused an incident that made the pipeline fail, blocking new deployments for several hours. A DevOps engineer must ensure that only the pipeline can perform deployments in the production environment. The DevOps engineer must also be able to access the environment in an emergency. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Update the DevOps group to have the ReadOnlyAccess permission set for the production accounts. Configure the DevOps engineer user with a new permission set that has AdministratorAccess permissions and that allows the user to assume the pipeline role. Add an SCP that denies modification of resources by any entity other than the pipeline role.

B. Create an SCP that denies all write actions for the DevOps team members on the production OU. Configure a new user in IAM Identity Center for the DevOps engineer with a new permission set that has AdministratorAccess permissions. Add an SCP that denies modification of resources by any entity other than the pipeline role.

C. Update the DevOps group to be able to assume the pipeline role for the production accounts. Configure a new user in IAM Identity Center for the DevOps engineer with a new permission set that has AdministratorAccess permissions. Add an SCP that denies modification of resources by any entity other than the DevOps engineer.

D. Create an SCP that denies all write actions for the DevOps team members on the production OU. Use a specific tag to tag the resources that CodePipeline provisions. Add an SCP that denies modification of tagged resources by any entity other than the DevOps engineer.
questions.explanation: An SCP attached to the production OU can impose an explicit deny on resource modifications for every principal except the pipeline role. Assigning the DevOps group read-only production access prevents normal team members from making production changes. A separate emergency AdministratorAccess permission set for the designated engineer, with permission to assume the pipeline role, provides emergency access through the sole role exempted by the SCP. SCPs set the maximum permissions for principals in affected member accounts, and an explicit SCP deny overrides otherwise granted IAM permissions.

Manage AWS accounts with permission sets

questions.questionText: AnyCompany uses AWS Organizations to create and manage multiple AWS accounts. AnyCompany recently acquired a smaller company, Example Corp. As part of the acquisition, Example Corp's single AWS account joined AnyCompany's management account through an Organizations invitation. AnyCompany moved the new member account into an OU dedicated to Example Corp. AnyCompany's DevOps engineer has an IAM user that assumes a role named OrganizationAccountAccessRole to access member accounts. This role is configured with a full-access policy. When the DevOps engineer attempts to use the AWS Management Console to assume the role in Example Corp's new member account, the DevOps engineer receives this error message: "Invalid information in one or more fields. Check your information or contact your administrator." Which solution will provide the DevOps engineer with access to the new member account?
options: A. In the management account, grant the DevOps engineer's IAM user permission to assume the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the new member account.

B. In the management account, create a new SCP. In the SCP, grant the DevOps engineer's IAM user full access to all resources in the new member account. Attach the SCP to the OU that contains the new member account.

C. In the new member account, create a new IAM role that is named OrganizationAccountAccessRole. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy to the role. In the role's trust policy, grant the management account permission to assume the role.
D. In the new member account, edit the trust policy for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role. Grant the management account permission to assume the role.
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations does not automatically create OrganizationAccountAccessRole in an existing account that joins an organization by invitation. The invited member account must have that cross-account role created manually, with the AdministratorAccess managed policy attached and a trust policy that permits the management account to assume it. Creating OrganizationAccountAccessRole for an invited account with AWS Organizations

Managing account invitations with AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is evaluating the lowest-cost approach to build an image batch-processing cluster on AWS. The application cannot operate in Docker containers and must run on Amazon EC2. The batch job saves checkpoint data to an NFS volume and can tolerate interruptions. Setting up the cluster software from a generic EC2 Linux image requires 30 minutes. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
options: A. Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. To complete the job, use an EC2 Auto Scaling group and an On-Demand pricing model to provision EC2 instances temporarily.
B. Use GlusterFS on EC2 instances for checkpoint data. To run the batch job, configure EC2 instances manually. When the job completes, shut down the instances manually.
C. Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. Use EC2 Fleet to launch EC2 Spot Instances, and utilize user data to configure the EC2 Linux instance on startup.
D. Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. Use EC2 Fleet to launch EC2 Spot Instances. Create a custom AMI for the cluster and use the latest AMI when creating instances.
questions.explanation: EC2 Spot Instances minimize compute cost for interruption-tolerant batch work. Amazon EFS provides managed, scalable shared file storage that EC2 Linux instances can mount through NFS, allowing checkpoint data to persist independently of interrupted instances. A custom AMI with the cluster software preconfigured eliminates the repeated 30-minute startup configuration cost, making Spot capacity launched through EC2 Fleet more cost-effective.

Use Amazon EFS with Amazon EC2 Linux instances

questions.questionText: A company runs sensitive workloads across AWS accounts that belong to the company’s AWS Organizations organization. The company uses an IP address range to allocate IP addresses for Amazon VPC CIDR blocks and all non-cloud hardware. The company requires a solution that prevents principals outside the company’s IP address range from taking AWS actions in the organization’s accounts. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Firewall Manager for the organization. Create an AWS Network Firewall policy that allows only source traffic from the company's IP address range. Set the policy scope to all accounts in the organization.
B. In Organizations, create an SCP that denies source IP addresses that are outside of the company’s IP address range. Attach the SCP to the organization's root.
C. Configure Amazon GuardDuty for the organization. Create a GuardDuty trusted IP address list for the company's IP range. Activate the trusted IP list for the organization.
D. In Organizations, create an SCP that allows source IP addresses that are inside of the company’s IP address range. Attach the SCP to the organization's root.
questions.explanation: A service control policy attached to the organization root can impose an explicit organization-wide guardrail on all member accounts. A Deny statement for all actions with a NotIpAddress condition on aws:SourceIp explicitly denies requests from source IP addresses outside the approved company CIDR range; explicit denies override otherwise applicable IAM permissions. SCPs attached at the root affect the accounts beneath it.
learnMore: SCP evaluation

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company runs an internal application in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on Amazon… Question 268 / Configuration Management and IaC A company runs an internal application in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on Amazon EC2. The ECS cluster instances can access the public internet. The ECS tasks running on the cluster instances are configured to use images from both private Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories and a public ECR registry repository. A new security policy requires the company to eliminate the ECS cluster's direct internet access. The company must remove all NAT gateways and internet gateways from the VPC that hosts the cluster. A DevOps engineer must ensure that the ECS cluster can continue downloading images from both the public ECR registry and the private ECR repositories. Images from the public ECR registry must stay current. New image versions must be available to the ECS cluster within 24 hours after publication. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? Choose three
options: A. Create an AWS CodeBuild project and a new private ECR repository for each image that is downloaded from the public ECR registry. Configure each project to pull the image from the public ECR repository and push the image to the new private ECR repository. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the CodeBuild project once every 24 hours. Update each task definition in the ECS cluster to refer to the new private ECR repository.

B. Create a new Amazon ECR pull through cache rule for each image that is downloaded from the public ECR registry. Create an AWS Lambda function that invokes each pull through cache rule. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function once every 24 hours. Update each task definition in the ECS cluster to refer to the image from the pull through cache.

C. Create a new Amazon ECR pull through cache rule for the public ECR registry. Update each task definition in the ECS cluster to refer to the image from the pull through cache. Ensure each public image has been downloaded through the pull through cache at least once before removing internet access from the VPC.
D. Create an Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoint for the public ECR repositories that are in the VPC.
E. Create an Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoint for the private ECR repositories that are in the VPC.
questions.explanation: An Amazon ECR pull-through cache stores public-registry images in the private ECR registry. Once an image has been pulled through the cache, later pulls are served from the cache without internet access; Amazon ECR checks the upstream registry for updates after the 24-hour cache-validation period. Downloading each needed public image before removing egress prevents the initial cache population from requiring internet access. Amazon ECS tasks on EC2 require Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints for private ECR access and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint because ECR stores image layers in Amazon S3.
learnMore: Sync an upstream registry with an Amazon ECR private registry

questions.questionText: A company operates an application with an Amazon EC2 and on-premises setup. A DevOps engineer must standardize patching across both environments. Company policy requires patching to occur only during non-business hours. Which combination of actions will satisfy these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Add the physical machines into AWS Systems Manager using Systems Manager Hybrid Activations.
B. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instances, allowing them to be managed by AWS Systems Manager.
C. Create IAM access keys for the on-premises machines to interact with AWS Systems Manager.
D. Run an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to patch the systems every hour
E. Use Amazon EventBridge scheduled events to schedule a patch window.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Hybrid Activations register on-premises servers as managed nodes, while an IAM role attached to each EC2 instance grants Systems Manager the permissions required to manage it. Systems Manager Maintenance Windows define scheduled periods for potentially disruptive operations such as operating-system patching, allowing the patch task to run only during non-business hours.
learnMore: Managing EC2 instances with Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A media company runs several thousand Amazon EC2 instances in an AWS account. The company uses Slack and a shared email inbox for team communications and important updates. A DevOps engineer must send every AWS-scheduled EC2 maintenance notification to the Slack channel and the shared inbox. The solution must include each instance’s Name and Owner tags. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Integrate AWS Trusted Advisor with AWS Config. Configure a custom AWS Config rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to publish notifications to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe a Slack channel endpoint and the shared inbox to the topic.

B. Use Amazon EventBridge to monitor for AWS Health events. Configure the maintenance events to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to send notifications to the Slack channel and the shared inbox.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function that sends EC2 maintenance notifications to the Slack channel and the shared inbox. Monitor EC2 health events by using Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Configure a CloudWatch alarm that invokes the Lambda function when a maintenance notification is received.

D. Configure AWS Support integration with AWS CloudTrail. Create a CloudTrail lookup event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to pass EC2 maintenance notifications to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Configure Amazon SNS to target the Slack channel and the shared inbox.
questions.explanation: AWS Health sends account-specific EC2 scheduled-maintenance events to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can route those events to Amazon SNS, which can invoke a Lambda function. The function can use the affected EC2 instance identifiers to retrieve the Name and Owner tags, enrich the notification, and deliver it to Slack and the shared email inbox. Amazon EC2 scheduled events are specifically monitored through AWS Health and EventBridge, rather than CloudWatch metrics, Trusted Advisor, or CloudTrail lookups.
learnMore: Scheduled events for Amazon EC2 instances

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application writes a log file that captures the username, date, time, and source IP address for each login. The log is published to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The company is conducting a root cause analysis for an event that took place on the previous day. The company needs to determine the number of logins for a particular user during the past 7 days. Which solution will provide this information?
options: A. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the log group. Use a filter pattern that matches the username. Publish a CloudWatch metric that sums the number of logins over the past 7 days.
B. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription on the log group. Use a filter pattern that matches the username. Publish a CloudWatch metric that sums the number of logins over the past 7 days.
C. Create a CloudWatch Logs Insights query that uses an aggregation function to count the number of logins for the username over the past 7 days. Run the query against the log group.
D. Create a CloudWatch dashboard. Add a number widget that has a filter pattern that counts the number of logins for the username over the past 7 days directly from the log group.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs Insights can run a query against the log group for the past 7 days, filter events for the specified username, and use an aggregation such as stats count(*) to return the number of matching login events. AWS documents that the stats command calculates aggregate statistics and that count() counts log events returned by a query.
learnMore: stats - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
CloudWatch Logs Insights language query syntax

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer finds that every Amazon EC2 instance running behind an Application Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group is not responding to user requests. The EC2 instances are also failing the target group's HTTP health checks. After investigating, the engineer finds that the application process is not running on any EC2 instance. The system logs contain a significant number of out-of-memory messages. The engineer must improve application resilience to handle a potential application memory leak. Monitoring and notifications must be enabled to provide alerts when an issue occurs. Which combination of actions meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Change the Auto Scaling configuration to replace the instances when they fail the load balancer's health checks.
B. Change the target group health check HealthCheckIntervalSeconds parameter to reduce the interval between health checks.
C. Change the target group health checks from HTTP to TCP to check if the port where the application is listening is reachable.

D. Enable the available memory consumption metric within the Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for the entire Auto Scaling group. Create an alarm when the memory utilization is high. Associate an Amazon SNS topic to the alarm to receive notifications when the alarm goes off.

E. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to collect the memory utilization of the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group. Create an alarm when the memory utilization is high and associate an Amazon SNS topic to receive a notification.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can be configured to use Elastic Load Balancing health checks; when the load balancer reports a registered instance as unhealthy, Auto Scaling marks it unhealthy and replaces it. Memory utilization is not an EC2 default metric, but the CloudWatch agent collects host memory metrics from each EC2 instance. A CloudWatch alarm on that metric can send notifications through an Amazon SNS topic.
learnMore: About the health checks for your Auto Scaling group
Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent

questions.questionText: A company has enabled Amazon RDS storage autoscaling for its RDS DB instances. A DevOps team must visualize the autoscaling events on an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard. Which solution satisfies this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to RDS storage autoscaling events from RDS events. Create an AWS Lambda function that publishes a CloudWatch custom metric. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function. Visualize the custom metric by using the CloudWatch dashboard.

B. Create a trail by using AWS CloudTrail with management events configured. Configure the trail to send the management events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a metric filter in CloudWatch Logs to match the RDS storage autoscaling events. Visualize the metric filter by using the CloudWatch dashboard.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to RDS storage autoscaling events from the RDS events. Create a CloudWatch alarm. Configure the EventBridge rule to change the status of the CloudWatch alarm. Visualize the alarm status by using the CloudWatch dashboard.

D. Create a trail by using AWS CloudTrail with data events configured. Configure the trail to send the data events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a metric filter in CloudWatch Logs to match the RDS storage autoscaling events. Visualize the metric filter by using the CloudWatch dashboard.
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS delivers its events to Amazon EventBridge in near real time, and an EventBridge rule can invoke an AWS Lambda function for matching DB-instance events. The function can convert each storage-autoscaling event into a CloudWatch custom metric; custom metrics can be displayed on a CloudWatch dashboard. CloudTrail is intended to record API calls and related account activity, rather than serve as the source of RDS-generated autoscaling event notifications.
learnMore: Creating a rule that triggers on an Amazon RDS event
Monitoring Amazon RDS events

questions.questionText: A global company hosts its product catalog website in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company needs to improve website performance for users in different geographical Regions and reduce load on the origin server. The company must deploy a highly available cross-Region solution that uses Amazon CloudFront. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Set up multiple CloudFront distributions. Point each distribution to another S3 bucket in a different Region. Use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to direct users to the nearest distribution. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and the S3 bucket in the different Region.

B. Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in us-east-1. Configure global edge locations. Set up cache behaviors with optimal TTLs for static content and dynamic content. Configure origin failover to an S3 bucket in a different Region. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and the S3 bucket in the different Region.

C. Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in us-east-1. Configure Amazon ElastiCache clusters in multiple Regions to serve as a distributed caching layer between CloudFront and the S3 origin. Set up a replication script to synchronize the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to an S3 bucket in a different Region. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule the script to run once a day.

D. Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in the eu-west-1 Region. Configure Regional edge caches. Implement AWS Global Accelerator to route requests to the nearest Regional edge location. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and an S3 bucket in a different Region.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront provides global edge delivery, and Origin Shield adds a centralized caching layer that consolidates requests from CloudFront caching layers before they reach the S3 origin, thereby reducing origin load. Configuring an origin group with a replicated S3 bucket in another Region enables managed origin failover for high availability. Using one distribution, S3 replication, Origin Shield, cache behaviors, and CloudFront origin failover requires less operational management than maintaining multiple distributions, Route 53 routing, custom replication scripts, ElastiCache clusters, or Global Accelerator.
learnMore: Use Amazon CloudFront Origin Shield
Optimize high availability with CloudFront origin failover

questions.questionText: A company operates several AWS accounts, with an Amazon Connect instance running in each account. For event handling, the company uses the Amazon EventBridge default event bus in every account. A DevOps team must receive all Amazon Connect events in one central DevOps account. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in each account to allow the DevOps account to replay events. Configure an EventBridge rule in the DevOps account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the default event bus in the other accounts.

B. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in each account to allow the DevOps account to receive events. Configure an EventBridge rule in the DevOps account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the default event bus in the other accounts.

C. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in the DevOps account. Update the policy to allow events to be received from the accounts. Configure an EventBridge rule in each account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the DevOps account's default event bus.

D. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in the DevOps account. Update the policy to allow events to be replayed by the accounts. Configure an EventBridge rule in each account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the DevOps account's default event bus.
questions.explanation: For cross-account EventBridge event delivery, the receiving event bus must have a resource-based policy that permits the source accounts to send events. Each source account then uses an EventBridge rule that matches its Amazon Connect events and targets the default event bus in the DevOps account. Event replay is not part of cross-account event routing. Sending and receiving events between AWS accounts in Amazon EventBridge

Each source account then uses an EventBridge rule that matches its Amazon Connect events and targets the default event bus in the DevOps account.
